<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Investment Process </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser employs a disciplined, multi-stage investment process designed to identify, evaluate, structure, execute, and monitor investments
consistent with the Fund&#8217;s investment objective and strategy. Each stage of the process is described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 1:
Origination and Sourcing </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund, through the Adviser, expects to source opportunities through a multi-channel origination
approach, including relationships with corporate management teams, intermediaries, and other market participants. The Adviser expects to source opportunities through three principal channels: (i)&nbsp;the Sagard investment team&#8217;s existing
relationships and a broad network of banks, broker-dealers, accountants, lawyers, and other channels, including engagement with a database of over 350 middle market brokers and other vendors; (ii)&nbsp;the Sagard ecosystem, including PCC; and
(iii)&nbsp;referrals and opportunity sharing across Sagard&#8217;s multi-asset-class platform. The Adviser may also source opportunities through third-party channels, which may involve compensation paid to such third parties. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 2: Initial Screening and Pipeline Management </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Sagard investment team reviews hundreds of opportunities annually, reviewing each opportunity for fit with the Fund&#8217;s requirements,
strategy, and objectives, and the team typically meets formally three times per week to review pipeline opportunities and determine next steps. Senior members of the investment team review opportunities in the initial stages, enabling quick
identification and rejection of transactions that do not fit the Fund&#8217;s objectives. Opportunities that pass the initial screen proceed to a more detailed preliminary review. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 3: Preliminary Analysis &#8212; Posting Memo </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If an opportunity warrants further analysis, the deal team prepares a &#8220;Posting Memo&#8221; highlighting risks, merits, proposed diligence
plan, and preliminary structure, drawing on preliminary analysis from bidder materials and data rooms, publicly available information, management projections, and industry and management calls, and presents it to the broader investment team and
other relevant investment professionals for discussion and feedback. From entry into the process through the final Investment Committee decision, the deal team maintains a &#8220;Threads&#8221; document tracking questions raised at screening
meetings and updates answers as information develops throughout the diligence process. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 4: Term Sheet and Exclusivity
</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If the investment team concludes that an opportunity may meet the Fund&#8217;s investment objectives, the team will generally seek
to propose a formal term sheet that includes transaction exclusivity and reimbursement of legal and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">out-of-pocket</FONT></FONT> expenses by the issuer, although the Adviser does not
always obtain exclusivity and, in certain transactions, may proceed without it. Execution of a term sheet marks the commencement of full, exclusive due diligence. The Investment Committee is consulted on the proposed terms and structure prior to
issuance of a formal term sheet. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 5: Full Due Diligence </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Following execution of exclusivity, the Adviser conducts comprehensive, private equity-style due diligence on each prospective investment. The
relevant portfolio manager oversees due diligence and documentation; the team meets with management multiple times; the Adviser typically engages third-party experts; outside law firms are retained for legal diligence and documentation; and an
accounting firm is typically engaged to prepare a &#8220;quality of earnings&#8221; report for private companies, and background checks are conducted on key principals. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">28 </P>

</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">
<h5 align="left" style="font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Typical diligence workstreams include: base case, upside, and downside financial forecasts;
customer, supplier, and competitor diligence, including use of expert networks; review of material contracts; technical reports and third-party audits as needed; legal review encompassing existing litigation, regulatory matters, and collateral
analysis; a quality of earnings report from an accounting firm; management and professional references; and background investigations of key principals. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 6: Structuring and Documentation </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser structures and negotiates strict and comprehensive credit agreements intended to allow minimal leakage of cash and collateral and
to ensure asset coverage, and expects to include financial maintenance covenants to enable early engagement in the event of deteriorating performance. Transactions are expected to include an excess cash flow sweep; coupons are typically floating;
and the Adviser does not intend to focus on covenant-lite transactions. Security documentation is negotiated to provide first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the borrower and, in applicable structures, pledges of equity interests in
the borrower and its subsidiaries. Unusual or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-standard</FONT> documentation terms identified during the documentation process are escalated to the Investment Committee for review and approval prior to closing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 7: Investment Committee Approval </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">After diligence and documentation are substantially complete, the investment team prepares a final Investment Committee memorandum and proceeds
to final approval. The Investment Committee reviews each investment memo with business findings that are presented along with a discussion around operating and financial scenarios, including downside cases. On average, investment opportunities are
presented to the Investment Committee three to five times throughout the process, and no investment is made without majority approval of eligible voting members of the Investment Committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 8: Portfolio Monitoring and Risk Management </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Following investment, the Fund expects to actively monitor portfolio investments through ongoing review of financial reporting and covenant
compliance and regular engagement with management (and, where applicable, sponsors), with a focus on early identification of issues and proactive risk management consistent with the Fund&#8217;s capital preservation focus. Sagard&#8217;s investment
team monitors investments closely through, among other things, periodic calls with executives, weekly credit-manager calls, monthly &#8220;watch-list&#8221; meetings, and quarterly portfolio review sessions, with an iterative and proactive portfolio
management process. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser assigns an internal credit rating or risk classification to each portfolio investment at origination and
updates such ratings periodically and upon any material change in a portfolio company&#8217;s financial condition or operating performance. Investments demonstrating signs of deterioration or that breach financial covenants are placed on heightened
monitoring status and subject to more frequent review by senior investment professionals and the Investment Committee. The Adviser will work proactively with portfolio company management and, where applicable, financial sponsors, to address issues
as they arise, and will use available legal and structural remedies &#8212; including enforcement of covenants, exercise of lender rights, and, where necessary, restructuring or workout processes &#8212; in the interest of preserving and maximizing
recoveries. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">29 </P>

</DIV></Center>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stage 9: Exits </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser expects that the Fund will seek to exit most or all investments through borrower refinancing or dispositions of the borrower, and
active monitoring is used to determine if an exit may be necessary due to deterioration in fundamentals or industry challenges. There can be no assurance that any such exit opportunities will ultimately be available for Fund investments. The Adviser
will evaluate exit alternatives on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">case-by-case</FONT></FONT> basis with a view toward maximizing recoveries and returns to shareholders consistent with the Fund&#8217;s investment
objective. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Responsible Investment Policy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sagard is a signatory to the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment. Sagard is committed to promoting responsible investment
practices through the integration of environmental, social and governance (&#8220;<U>ESG</U>&#8221;) considerations, where appropriate, within the investment lifecycle across all investment strategies. Sagard believes that by incorporating
financially material ESG considerations into its investment where relevant and active ownership activities, Sagard can accelerate the development of its portfolio companies and create sustainable value and business resiliency. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sagard&#8217;s Responsible Investment Policy, as amended, restated or supplemented from time to time (&#8220;<U>Sagard&#8217;s RI
Policy</U>&#8221;), provides a broad framework for Sagard&#8217;s responsible investment approach across all investment strategies. The guidelines provided by Sagard&#8217;s RI Policy also govern the integration of ESG factors within the investment
process of each business line. Such guidelines allow for each business line to adopt an ESG policy that is best suited to its respective asset class and investment philosophy (as amended, restated or supplemented from time to time, the
&#8220;<U>Business Line RI Policy</U>&#8221;). The Fund excludes certain industries and sectors from consideration pursuant to its Business Line RI Policy, including oil, mining, chemicals and gas and exploration. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While we may consider such <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ESG-related</FONT> factors when making an investment decision in the same way we
consider other business-relevant topics that we consider most significant for maximizing and protecting value, it should not be assumed that any ESG initiatives, standards, or metrics described herein will apply to each asset in which the Fund
invests or that they have applied to each of the Fund&#8217;s prior investments. ESG is only one of many considerations that the Adviser takes into account when making investment decisions, and other considerations can be expected in certain
circumstances to outweigh ESG considerations. The information provided herein is intended solely to provide an indication of the ESG initiatives and standards that Sagard applies when seeking to evaluate and/or improve the sustainability
characteristics of an investment as part of the larger goal of maximizing financial returns on investments. Accordingly, certain investments may exhibit characteristics that are inconsistent with the initiatives, standards, or metrics described
herein. </P>

managed funds and investment vehicles, each of whose investment adviser is the Adviser or an investment adviser controlling, controlled by or under common control with the Adviser (and including any direct or indirect, wholly- or majority-owned
subsidiary of the Adviser or its affiliates), to participate in negotiated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> transactions where doing so is consistent with regulatory requirements and other pertinent factors, and pursuant to the
conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order. We expect that the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order will require, among other things, that allocations be &#8220;fair and
equitable&#8221; to us and that the Adviser (or the applicable investment adviser) considers the interests of us and any other affiliated 1940 <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Act-regulated</FONT> funds that rely on the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order in allocations. Under the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order, among other requirements, the terms, conditions, price, class of securities to be
purchased in respect of a particular investment, the date on which such investment is to be made and any registration rights applicable thereto, will generally be required to be the same for us and each other participating affiliated entity. The
requirements of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order (including any requirements for board approval thereunder), as well as other regulatory requirements associated with us and any other affiliated 1940 <FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Allocation Policy </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser and its affiliates currently perform investment advisory services that are similar to those it performs for the Fund for other
funds, accounts, investment vehicles or arrangements managed, sponsored, or advised by the Adviser and its affiliates, including proprietary or principal accounts and separately managed accounts for institutional clients (&#8220;<U>Other Sagard
Accounts</U>&#8221;), as well as to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> vehicles and arrangements formed to enable limited partners of certain Other Sagard Accounts, or third parties, to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-invest</FONT> alongside the Fund or Other Sagard Accounts (&#8220;<U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investors</FONT></U>&#8221;, and together with Other Sagard Accounts, the &#8220;<U>Other
Accounts</U>&#8221;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser has established an allocation policy with respect to the allocation of investment opportunities among
the Fund and the Other Sagard Accounts. The Adviser&#8217;s allocation policies, which are subject to constraints under the 1940 Act, will seek to ensure equitable allocation of investment opportunities among the Fund and other clients over time.<I>
</I>In allocating investment opportunities among the Fund and Other Sagard Accounts, the Adviser is expected to determine eligibility and appropriateness based on applicable investment objectives, strategies, structures, and governing documents, and
may identify additional factors restricting allocation, including, subject to applicable law and the conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order, the factors described below. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser is expected to allocate investment opportunities among eligible vehicles in its discretion, taking into account its allocation
policy and a range of factors that include, among others: the Fund&#8217;s and Other Sagard Accounts&#8217; investment objectives, policies, restrictions and guidelines (including term, investment period, and geographic, diversification and
concentration restrictions); the amount of capital required to fund the investment opportunity and current and projected available capital and borrowing capacity; undrawn capital available for investment; transaction sourcing; targeted rate of
return and investment holding period; the ability to accommodate structural, timing and other aspects of the investment opportunity; timing necessary to execute the investment; existing portfolio construction and diversification; the size, liquidity
and duration of the investment opportunity; stage of development of the prospective portfolio company and anticipated holding period; portfolio composition and concentration parameters (including geography, industry, issuer, volatility and
leverage); suitability as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">follow-on</FONT> investment for an existing portfolio company; use of leverage in the proposed capital structure; availability of other suitable investments; supply and demand for the
investment opportunity at a given price level; risk considerations; industry and other allocation targets; minimum and maximum investment size requirements; tax and accounting implications; current and anticipated market conditions; potential
conflicts of interest arising from more than one Fund or Other Sagard Account pursuing the same opportunity; any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;ramp-up&#8221;</FONT> period; any priority obligations to offer opportunities; related
investments; any tax, legal or regulatory restrictions deemed relevant by the Adviser; any other factors described in the Adviser&#8217;s allocation policy or Form ADV; any other relevant limitations in the governing documents of the Fund or Other
Sagard Accounts; and any other factors deemed relevant by the Adviser in the exercise of its judgment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Portions of any investment
opportunity not allocated to the Fund or Other Sagard Accounts may be offered as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> opportunities to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investors,</FONT> strategic partners or others in the
Adviser&#8217;s discretion. In addition, the Adviser and its affiliates from time to time provide certain investors in Other Sagard Accounts or third parties with contractual rights to participate in
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> opportunities alongside the Fund, and there will be times where a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investor</FONT> or Other Sagard Account will invest alongside the Fund in the same
transaction or, where the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investor</FONT> or Other Sagard Account holds priority or other contractual <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> rights, will receive an allocation of an investment
opportunity ahead of, or to the exclusion of, an allocation to the Fund, subject in each case to the 1940 Act, the conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order (once obtained) and the Adviser&#8217;s
allocation policy. This could result in the Fund not participating in an investment opportunity at all or participating to a lesser extent than it otherwise would have. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Competition </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The middle market private credit market is highly competitive, and the Fund expects to face significant competition in sourcing, evaluating,
and executing investment opportunities. The Fund will encounter competition from other entities with similar investment objectives, including a broad spectrum of lenders and sources of capital, many of which may have more relevant experience, more
personnel, greater financial resources, and greater willingness to take on risk, and may be more well-established than the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The
Fund&#8217;s competitors include, without limitation, other business development companies, private credit funds, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">closed-end</FONT> funds, hedge funds, insurance companies, banks and bank holding companies,
commercial finance companies, and, to a lesser extent, private equity funds and mezzanine funds that also provide debt capital to middle market companies. The Adviser believes that the sponsor-backed private credit market in particular has become
increasingly crowded and commoditized, resulting in highly competitive direct lending in the sponsor market and causing yield compression, increased leverage, and deterioration in credit terms and documentation. Many of the Fund&#8217;s competitors
are not subject to the regulatory constraints imposed on BDCs under the 1940 Act, including the asset coverage requirements and affiliated transaction restrictions applicable to the Fund, and may therefore be able to pursue a broader range of
investment strategies or employ higher levels of leverage than the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Competition may increase and could reduce the number of
investment opportunities available to the Fund and/or adversely affect the terms on which investments are made, which may reduce returns to shareholders, and it is possible the Fund may never be fully invested if insufficient attractive investment
opportunities are identified. Increased competition may also result in a reduction in yield premiums, weakened covenant protections, greater borrower-friendly structural concessions, and a general deterioration in the terms on which private credit
investments can be made. There can be no assurance that the competitive pressures facing the Fund will not adversely affect its ability to achieve its investment objective. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Brokerage Allocation and Other Practices </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Since we will generally acquire and dispose of our investments in privately negotiated transactions, we will infrequently use brokers in the
normal course of our business. Subject to policies established by the Board, if any, the Adviser will be primarily responsible for the execution of any publicly-traded securities portfolio transactions and the allocation of brokerage commissions.
The Adviser does not expect to execute transactions through any particular broker or dealer, but will seek to obtain the best net results for us, taking into account such factors as price (including the applicable brokerage commission or dealer
spread), size of order, difficulty of execution, and operational facilities of Sagard and Sagard&#8217;s risk and skill in positioning blocks of securities. While the Adviser generally will seek reasonably competitive trade execution costs, we will
not necessarily pay the lowest spread or commission available. Subject to applicable legal requirements, the Adviser may select a broker based partly upon brokerage or research services provided to it and us and any other clients. In return for such
services, we may pay a higher commission than other brokers would charge if the Adviser determines in good faith that such commission is reasonable in relation to the services provided. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Management Agreements </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Investment Advisory
Agreement </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Advisory Agreement, the Adviser will provide us with investment advisory services necessary for the
Fund&#8217;s business. Under the Advisory Agreement, the Fund will pay the Adviser fees for investment management services consisting of a base management fee (the &#8220;<U>Base Management Fee</U>&#8221;) and an incentive fee (the
&#8220;<U>Incentive Fee</U>&#8221;), in each case commencing on and after the BDC Election Date. Pursuant to a separate fee waiver letter agreement, the Adviser has agreed to waive, in part, the Base Management Fee during the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> period following the BDC Election Date (the &#8220;<U>Advisory Fee Waiver Period</U>&#8221;), as more fully described in &#8220;Compensation of Adviser &#8212; Base Management Fee&#8221; below. The Advisory
Fee Waiver Period is not automatically renewable, and there is no assurance the Adviser will agree to any extension or replacement fee waiver following its expiration. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to a separate fee waiver letter agreement, the Adviser has agreed to waive the
portion of the Base Management Fee in excess of 0.85% per annum of the Fund&#8217;s average monthly net assets for the Advisory Fee Waiver Period (the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> period following the BDC Election Date), such
that the effective Base Management Fee rate during the Advisory Fee Waiver Period will be 0.85% per annum. No portion of the Base Management Fee waived during the Advisory Fee Waiver Period is subject to recoupment by the Adviser. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Incentive Fee </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Incentive Fee consists
of two components that are independent of each other, with the result that one component may be payable even if the other is not. A portion of the incentive fee is based on a percentage of our income and a portion is based on a percentage of our
capital gains, each as described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Incentive Fee Based on Income </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The first part of the Incentive Fee, referred to as the &#8220;<U>Income Incentive Fee</U>,&#8221; will be calculated and payable quarterly in
arrears, commencing with the first full calendar quarter after the BDC Election Date, based on the Fund&#8217;s &#8220;<U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income</U>&#8221; for the immediately preceding
quarter (or portion thereof with respect to the quarter in which the BDC Election Date occurs). The payment of the Income Incentive Fee will be subject to a quarterly hurdle rate, expressed as a rate of return on the value of the Fund&#8217;s net
assets at the end of the most recently completed calendar quarter, of 1.25% (5.0% annualized) (the &#8220;<U>Hurdle Rate</U>&#8221;), subject to a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;catch-up&#8221;</FONT> feature (as described below). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For this purpose, &#8220;<U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income</U>&#8221; means interest income,
distribution/dividend income and any other income (including any other fees (other than fees for providing managerial assistance) such as commitment, origination, structuring, diligence and consulting fees or other fees that the Fund receives from
portfolio companies) accrued during the calendar quarter, minus the Fund&#8217;s operating expenses accrued for the quarter (including the Base Management Fee, costs and expenses payable or reimbursed to the Adviser under the Administration
Agreement, and any interest expense or fees on any credit facilities or outstanding debt and dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred shares, but excluding the Incentive Fee and any shareholder servicing and/or distribution fees). <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as market or original issue discount, debt instruments with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">payment-in-kind</FONT></FONT> interest, preferred stock investments with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">payment-in-kind</FONT></FONT> dividends, and
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">zero-coupon</FONT> securities), accrued income that the Fund has not yet received in cash. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income does not include any realized capital gains,
realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation. The impact of expense support payments and recoupments is also excluded from <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will pay the Adviser an Income Incentive Fee quarterly in arrears with respect to our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT>
Fee Net Investment Income in each calendar quarter as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">You should be aware that a rise in the general level of interest rates can be expected to
lead to higher interest rates applicable to our debt investments. Accordingly, an increase in interest rates would make it easier for us to meet or exceed the incentive fee hurdle rate and may result in a substantial increase in the amount of
incentive fees payable to the Adviser with respect to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income. Because of the structure of the incentive fee, it is possible that we may pay an Incentive Fee in a calendar
quarter in which we incur an overall loss taking into account capital account losses. For example, if we receive <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income in excess of the quarterly hurdle rate, we will pay the
applicable incentive fee even if we have incurred a loss in that calendar quarter due to realized and unrealized capital losses. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Incentive Fee Based on Capital Gains </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The second part of the Incentive Fee, referred to as the &#8220;<U>Capital Gains Incentive Fee</U>,&#8221; will be an incentive fee on capital
gains and will be determined and payable in arrears as of the end of each calendar year (or upon termination of the Advisory Agreement) commencing with the end of the first calendar year in which the BDC Election Date occurs. This fee will equal
12.5% of the Fund&#8217;s incentive fee capital gains, which will equal the Fund&#8217;s realized capital gains on a cumulative basis from the BDC Election Date, calculated as of the end of the applicable period, computed net of all realized capital
losses and unrealized capital depreciation on a cumulative basis from the BDC Election Date, less the aggregate amount of any previously paid Capital Gains Incentive Fee. For purposes of calculating the Capital Gains Incentive Fee under the Advisory
Agreement, the cost basis for any investment as of the BDC Election Date will be deemed to be the most recently determined fair value for such investment as of the BDC Election Date, determined in accordance with the Adviser&#8217;s valuation
policies and procedures. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On a quarterly basis, we will accrue for the capital gains incentive fee by calculating such fee as if it were
due and payable as of the end of such period. We will include unrealized gains in the calculation of the capital gains incentive fee expense and related accrued capital gains incentive fee. This accrual will reflect the incentive fees that would be
payable to the Adviser if our entire portfolio was liquidated at its fair value as of the balance sheet date even though the Adviser is not entitled to an incentive fee with respect to unrealized gains unless and until such gains are actually
realized. In no event will the capital gains incentive fee payable pursuant to the Advisory Agreement be in excess of the amount permitted by the Advisers Act, including Section&nbsp;205 thereof. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Any of the fees payable to the Adviser under the Advisory Agreement for any partial month or calendar quarter will be appropriately prorated.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Certain Terms of the Advisory Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Advisory Agreement has been approved by the Board. Unless earlier terminated as described below, the Advisory Agreement will remain in
effect for a period of two years from the date it first becomes effective and will remain in effect from <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-to-year</FONT></FONT> thereafter if approved annually by a majority of
the Board or by the holders of a majority of our outstanding voting securities and, in each case, a majority of the Directors who are not &#8220;interested persons,&#8221; as defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act, of the Fund
(&#8220;<U>Independent Directors</U>&#8221;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We may terminate the Advisory Agreement without payment of any penalty upon 60 days&#8217;
written notice. The decision to terminate the Advisory Agreement may be made by a majority of the Board or the shareholders holding a majority of our outstanding voting securities, which means the lesser of (1) 67% or more of the voting securities
present at a meeting if more than 50% of the outstanding voting securities are present or represented by proxy, or (2)&nbsp;more than 50% of the outstanding voting securities. In addition, without payment of any penalty, the Adviser may terminate
the Advisory Agreement upon 90 days&#8217; written notice. The Advisory Agreement will automatically terminate within the meaning of the 1940 Act and related SEC guidance and interpretations in the event of its assignment. Notwithstanding any
termination of the Advisory Agreement, the indemnification provisions described below will remain in full force and effect following such termination, and the Adviser will remain entitled to the benefits thereof. In addition, following any
termination or expiration of the Advisory Agreement, the Adviser will be entitled to any amounts owed under the Advisory Agreement through the date of termination or expiration. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Administration Agreement </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant
to the Administration Agreement, the Adviser will perform, or oversee or arrange for, the performance of, the administrative services necessary for our operations, including the provision of general ledger accounting, fund accounting, legal
services, investor relations, certain government and regulatory affairs activities, and other administrative services. The Adviser will also perform, or oversee the performance of, our corporate operations and required administrative services, which
includes being responsible for the financial records that we are required to maintain and preparing reports for our shareholders and reports filed with the SEC. In addition, the Adviser will assist us in calculating our NAV, overseeing the
preparation and filing of tax returns and the printing and dissemination of reports to our shareholders, and generally overseeing the payment of our expenses and the performance of administrative and professional services rendered to us by others.
The Adviser may delegate or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-contract</FONT> certain of its services under the Administration Agreement to other entities, including a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-administrator,</FONT> and has done so as
described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Administration Agreement, we reimburse the Adviser for expenses necessary to perform services related to
our administration and operations, including the Adviser&#8217;s allocable portion of the compensation and related expenses of certain personnel of Sagard and its affiliates providing administrative services to us on behalf of the Adviser. We
reimburse the Adviser for all costs and expenses incurred by the Adviser in performing its obligations and providing personnel and facilities under the Administration Agreement. The Adviser allocates the cost of such services to us based on factors
such as time spent (including on an estimated basis), assets under management, usage rates, proportionate holdings, a combination thereof or other reasonable methods. The Board will review the methodology employed in determining how the expenses are
allocated to us and the proposed allocation of administrative expenses among us and certain affiliates of the Adviser. The Board will then assess the reasonableness of such reimbursements for expenses allocated to us based on the breadth, depth and
quality of such services. In addition, the Board will compare the total amount paid to the Adviser for such services as a percentage of our net assets to the same ratio as reported by other comparable BDCs. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Administration Agreement will continue in effect for an initial period of two years from the date it first becomes effective, and
thereafter will continue automatically for successive annual periods, provided that such continuance is specifically approved at least annually by (i)&nbsp;the vote of a majority of the Board, or by the vote of a majority of the outstanding voting
securities of the Fund, and (ii)&nbsp;the vote of a majority of members of the Board who are not parties to the Administration Agreement or &#8220;interested persons&#8221; (as such term is defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act) of any
such party, in accordance with the requirements of the 1940 Act. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Administration Agreement may be terminated at any time, without the
payment of any penalty, (i)&nbsp;by the Fund, by the vote of a majority of the outstanding voting securities of the Fund or by the vote of a majority of the Fund&#8217;s directors, upon not less than 60 days&#8217; prior written notice to the
Adviser, or (ii)&nbsp;by the Adviser, upon not less than 90 days&#8217; prior written notice to the Fund. The Administration Agreement will also automatically terminate in the event of its &#8220;assignment&#8221; (as such term is defined for
purposes of Section&nbsp;15(a)(4) of the 1940&nbsp;Act). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund has agreed to indemnify the Adviser, in its capacity as administrator
for the Fund, against certain liabilities and expenses arising from the performance of the Adviser&#8217;s duties under the Administration Agreement, except for any liability arising from willful misfeasance, bad faith, gross negligence or reckless
disregard of the Adviser&#8217;s duties thereunder. In connection with indemnification claims, the Fund is required to advance expenses (including reasonable legal fees) to indemnified parties within 30 days of receipt of a request for such advance,
subject to undertakings to repay such amounts to the extent the indemnified party is ultimately determined not to be entitled to indemnification. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser has agreed to advance all of our organization and offering expenses on our
behalf (including legal, accounting, printing, mailing, subscription processing and filing fees and expenses and other offering expenses, including costs associated with technology integration between the Fund&#8217;s systems and those of our
participating brokers, reasonable bona fide due diligence expenses of participating brokers supported by detailed and itemized invoices, costs in connection with preparing sales materials and other marketing expenses, design and website expenses,
fees and expenses of our transfer agent, fees to attend retail seminars sponsored by participating brokers and costs, expenses and reimbursements for travel, meals, accommodations, entertainment and other similar expenses related to meetings or
events with prospective investors, brokers, registered investment advisors or financial or other advisors, but excluding the shareholder servicing and/or distribution fee) through December 31, 2026, and will pay for any such organization and
offering expenses in excess of $1.5&nbsp;million (the &#8220;O&amp;O Cap&#8221;) on our behalf without reimbursement or recoupment. We will be obligated to reimburse the Adviser for organization and offering expenses (up to the O&amp;O Cap) and any
other Expense Payments (as defined below) advanced by the Adviser pursuant to the Expense Support and Conditional Reimbursement Agreement we have entered into with the Adviser (the &#8220;<U>Expense Support Agreement</U>&#8221;) only if certain
conditions are met. See &#8220;<I>Item 1. Business&nbsp;&#8212; Management Agreements&nbsp;&#8212; Expense Support and Conditional</I> <I>Reimbursement Agreement.</I>&#8221; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Expense Support and Conditional Reimbursement Agreement </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have entered into the Expense Support Agreement with the Adviser, pursuant to which the Adviser (1)&nbsp;has agreed to advance or otherwise
bear all of our organization and offering expenses through December 31, 2026 and (2) may elect, in its discretion, to pay certain of our expenses on our behalf (each, an <U>&#8220;Expense Payment</U>&#8221;), provided that no portion of any Expense
Payment will be used to pay any interest expense or distribution and/or shareholder servicing fees of the Fund. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Expense Support Agreement, in no event will the Fund bear organization and offering
expenses in excess of the $1.5 million O&amp;O Cap; to the extent such expenses exceed the O&amp;O Cap, the Adviser will pay the excess on the Fund&#8217;s behalf without reimbursement or recoupment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund&#8217;s right to receive an Expense Payment becomes an asset of the Fund once the Adviser commits in writing to pay it. Any Expense
Payment that the Adviser has committed to pay must be paid by the Adviser to or on behalf of the Fund in any combination of cash or other immediately available funds no later than 45 days after such commitment was made in writing, and/or offset
against amounts due from us to the Adviser or its affiliates. The Adviser will be entitled to reimbursement of Expense Payments from us if Available Operating Funds (as defined below) exceed the cumulative distributions accrued to the Fund&#8217;s
shareholders, among other conditions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Beginning after December 31, 2026, following any calendar&nbsp;month (such calendar&nbsp;month, the
&#8220;<U>Applicable Calendar</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;Month</U>&#8221;) in which Available Operating Funds exceed the cumulative distributions accrued to the Fund&#8217;s shareholders based on distributions declared with respect to record dates occurring
in the Applicable Calendar&nbsp;Month (the amount of such excess being hereinafter referred to as &#8220;<U>Excess Operating</U> <U>Funds</U>&#8221;), we will pay such Excess Operating Funds, or a portion thereof, to the Adviser until such time as
all Expense Payments made by the Adviser to the Fund within three&nbsp;years prior to the last business day of the Applicable Calendar&nbsp;Month have been reimbursed. Any payments required to be made by the Fund shall be referred to herein as a
&#8220;<U>Reimbursement Payment</U>.&#8221; &#8220;<U>Available Operating Funds</U>&#8221; means the sum of (i)&nbsp;our net investment income calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP, (ii)&nbsp;our net capital gains (including the excess of net
long-term capital gains over net short-term capital losses) and (iii)&nbsp;dividends and other distributions paid to us on account of investments in portfolio companies (to the extent such amounts listed in clause (iii)&nbsp;are not included under
clauses (i)&nbsp;and (ii)&nbsp;above). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">No Reimbursement Payment for any Applicable Calendar Month shall be made if&nbsp;the Fund&#8217;s
Operating Expense Ratio at the time of such proposed Reimbursement Payment is greater than the Operating Expense Ratio at the time the Expense Payment was made to which such Reimbursement Payment relates. The &#8220;Operating Expense Ratio&#8221; is
calculated by dividing the Fund&#8217;s operating expenses, less organization and offering expenses, base management fees and incentive fees owed to the Adviser, shareholder servicing and/or distribution fees and interest expense, by the
Fund&#8217;s&nbsp;monthly average net assets. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">42 </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund&#8217;s obligation to make a Reimbursement Payment shall automatically become a
liability of the Fund on the last business day of the Applicable Calendar Month, except to the extent that the Adviser has waived its right to receive such payment for the applicable&nbsp;month. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Determination of Net Asset Value </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We
generally expect to determine our NAV for each class of Common Shares on a monthly basis as of the last day of each calendar month. The NAV per share for each class of Common Shares is determined by dividing the value of total assets attributable to
the class minus liabilities attributable to the class by the total number of Common Shares outstanding of the class at the date as of which the determination is made. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Valuation of Portfolio Investments </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We conduct the valuation of our investments, upon which our NAV is based, at all times consistent with GAAP and the 1940 Act. The Board is
responsible for overseeing the valuation of our portfolio investments at fair value as determined in good faith pursuant to the Adviser&#8217;s valuation policy. As permitted by Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2a-5</FONT> of the 1940 Act, the
Board has designated the Adviser as our valuation designee with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> responsibility for implementing the portfolio valuation process set forth in the
Adviser&#8217;s valuation policy. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We value our investments in accordance with FASB ASC 820, Fair Value Measurements (&#8220;<U>ASC
820</U>&#8221;) and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Rule&nbsp;2a-5</FONT> under the 1940&nbsp;Act, which defines fair value as the value of a portfolio investment for which market quotations are not readily available. A market quotation is
&#8220;readily available&#8221; only when it is a quoted price (unadjusted) in active markets for identical instruments that a fund can access at the measurement date, provided that such a quotation is not considered to be readily available if it is
not reliable. ASC 820 prioritizes the use of observable market prices derived from such prices over entity-specific inputs and establishes a three-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value. These tiers
include: Level&nbsp;1, defined as observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical securities; Level&nbsp;2, which includes inputs such as quoted prices for similar securities in active markets and quoted prices for identical
securities where there is little or no activity in the market; and Level&nbsp;3, defined as unobservable inputs for which little or no market data exists, therefore requiring an entity to develop its own assumptions. Due to the inherent
uncertainties of valuation, certain estimated fair values may differ significantly from the values that would have been realized had a readily available market quotation for these investments existed, and these differences could be material. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Investments for which market quotations are readily available will typically be valued at those market quotations. To validate market
quotations, we will utilize a number of factors to determine if the quotations are representative of fair value, including the source and number of the quotations. To assess the continuing appropriateness of pricing sources and methodologies, the
Adviser will regularly perform price verification procedures and issue challenges as necessary to independent pricing services or brokers, and any differences are reviewed in accordance with the valuation procedures. The Adviser will not adjust the
prices unless it has a reason to believe market quotations are not reflective of the fair value of an investment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Where prices or inputs
are not available or, in the judgment of the valuation designee, are not reliable, valuation techniques based on the facts and circumstances of the particular investment will be utilized. Securities that are not publicly traded or for which market
prices are not readily available, will be valued at fair value as determined in good faith by the Adviser, as the Fund&#8217;s valuation designee, with input by independent valuation firms engaged on the recommendation of the Adviser and at the
direction of the Board, and with oversight by the Board and its audit committee. These valuation approaches involve some level of management estimation and judgment, the degree of which is dependent on the price transparency for the investments or
market and the investments&#8217; complexity. Our Board may modify our valuation procedures from time to time. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">43 </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Determination of fair value involves subjective judgments and estimates. Accordingly, the notes to our consolidated financial statements that
will be included in our SEC filings will refer to the uncertainty with respect to the possible effect of such valuations and any change in such valuations on our consolidated financial statements. In making its determination of fair value, the
Adviser may use any independent third-party pricing or valuation services for which it has performed the appropriate level of due diligence. However, the Adviser is not required to determine fair value in accordance with the valuation provided by
any single source, and may use any relevant data, including information sourced by the Adviser or provided by any independent third-party valuation or pricing service that the Adviser deems to be reliable in determining fair value under the
circumstances. Below is a description of factors that the Adviser and any independent third-party valuation services may consider when determining the fair value of our investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As part of the valuation process, the Adviser will generally take into account relevant factors in determining the fair value of our
investments for which reliable market quotations are not readily available, many of which are loans, including and in combination, as relevant, of: (i)&nbsp;the portfolio company&#8217;s ability to make payments based on its earnings and cash flow,
(ii)&nbsp;the estimated enterprise value of a portfolio company, (iii)&nbsp;the nature and realizable value of any collateral, (iv)&nbsp;the markets in which the portfolio company does business, (v)&nbsp;a comparison of the portfolio company&#8217;s
securities to any similar publicly traded securities, and (vi)&nbsp;overall changes in the interest rate environment and the credit markets that may affect the price at which similar </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">44 </P>

investments may be made in the future. When an external event such as a purchase transaction, public offering or subsequent equity or debt sale occurs, the Adviser, with the assistance of
independent valuation firms and oversight by the Board and its audit committee, considers whether the pricing indicated by the external event corroborates its valuation. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">When the Adviser determines NAV as of the last day of a month that is not also the last day of a calendar quarter, we intend to update the
value of securities with reliable market quotations to the most recent market quotation. For securities without reliable market quotations, the Adviser&#8217;s valuation team will generally value such assets at the most recent quarterly valuation
unless the Adviser determines that a significant observable change has occurred since the most recent <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">quarter-end</FONT> with respect to the investment (which determination may be as a result of a material event at a
portfolio company, material change in market spreads, secondary market transaction in the securities of an investment or otherwise). If the Adviser determines such a change has occurred with respect to one or more investments, the Adviser will
determine whether to update the value for each relevant investment using a range of values from an independent valuation firm, where applicable, in accordance with the Adviser&#8217;s valuation policy, pursuant to authority designated by the Board.
Additionally, the Adviser may otherwise determine to update the most recent <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">quarter-end</FONT> valuation of an investment without reliable market quotations that the Adviser considers to be material to the Fund using
a range of values from an independent valuation firm. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Refer to the notes to our consolidated financial statements included in our future
SEC filings for additional information regarding the fair value of our financial instruments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Determination of NAV </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will use the valuation procedures set forth above in order to determine our NAV, as applied by the Adviser as our valuation designee under
Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2a-5</FONT> under the 1940 Act. Fair value pricing may require subjective determinations about the value of a security. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For purposes of calculating NAV, all assets and liabilities initially expressed in foreign currencies will be converted into U.S. dollars at
prevailing exchange rates as may be determined in good faith by the Adviser under the supervision of the Board. Although the Adviser&#8217;s policy is intended to result in a calculation of our NAV that fairly reflects security values as of the time
of pricing, we cannot ensure that fair values determined by the Adviser would accurately reflect the price that we could obtain for a security if it were to dispose of that security as of the time of pricing (for instance, in a forced or distressed
sale). The prices used by the Adviser when determining fair value may differ from the value that would be realized if the securities were sold. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The NAV calculation will generally be available within 20 business days after the end of the applicable month. Changes in our monthly NAV will
reflect factors including, but not limited to, accruals for net portfolio income, interest expense and unrealized/realized gains (losses) on assets, any applicable organization and offering costs and any expense reimbursements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The most recently determined NAV per share for the Common Shares will be reported by the Fund under cover of a Current Report on Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">8-K</FONT> filed with the SEC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Relationship between NAV and Our Transaction Price </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although the transaction price in the monthly closings for the Private Offering will generally be based on the NAV per share as of the last
calendar day of the prior month (plus any applicable sales load and placement agent fees), such transaction price may be significantly different from the prior subscription closing price per Common Share or the NAV per Common Share as of the date on
which the shareholder&#8217;s investment decision is made (or repurchase occurs), and therefore shareholders may receive a smaller number of Common Shares than if they had subscribed at the prior subscription closing price (or may receive a lesser
amount of proceeds than if they had submitted a repurchase request at the available NAV at the time the shareholder submitted such repurchase request). </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, we may offer Common Shares at a price that we believe reflects the NAV per
share more appropriately than the prior month&#8217;s NAV per share (including by updating a previously disclosed offering price) or suspend our offering in exceptional cases where we believe there has been a material change (positive or negative)
to our NAV per share since the end of the prior month due to the aggregate impact of factors such as general significant market events or disruptions or force majeure events. In cases where our transaction price is not based on the prior
month&#8217;s NAV per share, the offering price will not equal our NAV per share as of any time. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Limits on the Calculation of Our Per Share NAV
</I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although our primary goal in establishing our valuation guidelines is to produce a valuation that represents a reasonable estimate of
the market value of our investments, or the price that would be received upon the sale of our investments in market transactions, the methodologies used will be based on judgments, assumptions and opinions about future events that may or may not
prove to be correct, and if different judgments, assumptions or opinions were used, a different estimate would likely result. Furthermore, our published per share NAV may not fully reflect certain extraordinary events because we may not be able to
immediately quantify the financial impact of such events on our portfolio. The Adviser will monitor our portfolio between valuations to determine whether there have been any extraordinary events that may have materially changed the estimated market
value of the portfolio, such as significant market events or disruptions or force majeure events. If required by applicable securities law, we will promptly disclose the occurrence of such event under cover of a Current Report on Form <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">8-K</FONT> or other public disclosure, and the Adviser will analyze the impact of such extraordinary event on our portfolio and determine, in coordination with third-party valuation services, the appropriate adjustment to
be made to our NAV. We will not, however, retroactively adjust NAV. To the extent that the extraordinary events may result in a material change in value of a specific investment, the Adviser will order a new valuation of the investment, which will
be prepared by the third-party valuation service. It is not known whether any resulting disparity will benefit shareholders whose shares are or are not being repurchased or purchasers of our Common Shares. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We include no discounts to our NAV for the illiquid nature of our shares, including the limitations on the ability to sell shares under our
discretionary share repurchase program and our ability to suspend the share repurchase program at any time. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our NAV generally does not
consider exit costs that would likely be incurred if our assets and liabilities were liquidated or sold. While we may use market pricing concepts to value individual components of our NAV, our per share NAV is not derived from the market pricing
information of BDCs or other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">closed-end</FONT> investment companies on stock exchanges. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We do not
represent, warrant or guarantee that: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Exchange</FONT> Traded, Perpetual-Life BDC </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We intend to operate as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-exchange</FONT> traded, perpetual-life BDC, which is a BDC whose common shares
are not listed for trading on a stock exchange or other securities market. We use the term &#8220;perpetual-life BDC&#8221; to describe an investment vehicle of indefinite duration, whose common shares are intended to be sold by the BDC on a
continuous monthly basis at a price equal to the BDC&#8217;s then-current monthly NAV per share. In our perpetual-life structure, we may offer investors an opportunity to have their shares repurchased on a quarterly basis at NAV, but we are not
obligated to offer to repurchase any shares in any particular quarter in our discretion. We believe that our perpetual nature will enable us to execute a patient and opportunistic strategy and be able to invest across different market environments.
This may reduce the risk of the Fund being a forced seller of assets in market downturns compared to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-perpetual</FONT> funds. While we may consider a liquidity event at any time in the future, we currently do not
intend to undertake a liquidity event, and we are not obligated by our Organizational Documents or otherwise to effect a liquidity event at any time. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Emerging Growth Company </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will be an
&#8220;emerging growth company,&#8221; as defined by the JOBS Act. As an emerging growth company, we will be eligible to take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting and disclosure requirements that are applicable to public companies
that are not emerging growth companies. For so long as we remain an emerging growth company, we will not be required to, among other things, have an auditor attestation report on our internal control over financial reporting pursuant to
Section&nbsp;404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the JOBS Act provides that an emerging growth company may take advantage of
an extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards that have different effective dates for public and private companies. This means that an emerging growth company can delay adopting certain accounting standards
until such standards are otherwise applicable to private companies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will remain an emerging growth company until the earliest of: </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Employees </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We do not currently have any employees and do not expect to have any employees. Each of our executive officers described under &#8220;<I>Item
5. Directors and Executive Officers</I>&#8221; is a principal, officer or employee of the Adviser or its affiliates, which manages and oversees our investment operations. In the future, the Adviser may directly retain personnel based upon its needs.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Regulation as a BDC </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We intend to
elect to be treated as a BDC under the 1940 Act. In addition, following the BDC Election Date, we intend to, as soon as reasonably practicable, qualify and elect to be treated for federal income tax purposes, and intend to qualify annually
thereafter, as a RIC under the Code. Prior to its qualification as a RIC, the Fund will be taxed as a C-corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The 1940 Act contains prohibitions and restrictions relating to transactions between BDCs and
their affiliates, principal underwriters and affiliates of those affiliates or underwriters, as described below. A BDC must be organized in the United States for the purpose of investing in or lending to primarily private companies and making
significant managerial assistance available to them. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The 1940 Act also requires that a majority of the board of a BDC consist of persons
other than &#8220;interested persons,&#8221; as that term is defined in the 1940 Act. In addition, the 1940 Act provides that a BDC may not change the nature of its business so as to cease to be, or to withdraw its election as, a BDC unless approved
by a majority of the outstanding voting securities. The 1940 Act defines &#8220;a majority of the outstanding voting securities&#8221; as the lesser of (i) 67% or more of the voting securities present at a meeting if the holders of more than 50% of
our outstanding voting securities are present or represented by proxy or (ii) 50% of the outstanding voting securities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a BDC, we will
also generally not be able to issue and sell our Common Shares at a price per share, after deducting underwriting commissions and discounts, that is below our NAV per share. We may, however, sell our Common Shares, or warrants, options or rights to
acquire our Common Shares, at a price below the then-current NAV of our Common Shares if the Board determines that such sale is in our best interests and the best interests of our shareholders, and our shareholders approve such sale. In addition, we
may generally issue new shares of our Common Shares at a price below NAV per share in rights offerings to existing shareholders, in payment of dividends and in certain other limited circumstances. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following discussion is a general summary of the material prohibitions and descriptions governing BDCs generally and assumes that we have
filed our election to be regulated as a BDC under the 1940 Act. It does not purport to be a complete description of all of the laws and regulations affecting BDCs. </P>

least 70% of the company&#8217;s total assets. The principal categories of Qualifying Assets relevant to our business are any of the following: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

securities described in (1), (2) or (3)&nbsp;above. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Significant Managerial Assistance </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A BDC must have been organized and have its principal place of business in the United States and must be operated for the purpose of making
investments in the types of securities described above. However, in order to count portfolio securities as Qualifying Assets for the purpose of the 70% test, the BDC must either control the issuer of the securities or must offer to make available to
the issuer of the securities (other than small and solvent companies described above) significant managerial assistance; except that, where the BDC purchases such securities in conjunction with one or more other persons acting together, one of the
other persons in the group may make available such managerial assistance. Making available significant managerial assistance means, among other things, any arrangement whereby the BDC, through its directors, officers or employees, offers to provide
and, if accepted, does so provide, significant guidance and counsel concerning the management, operations or business objectives and policies of a portfolio company through monitoring of portfolio company operations, selective participation in board
and management meetings, consulting with and advising a portfolio company&#8217;s officers or other organizational or financial guidance. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Temporary Investments </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pending investment in other types of Qualifying Assets, as described above, our investments can consist of cash, cash equivalents, U.S.
