<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will be subject to financial market risks, including changes in interest rates. A rise in the general level of interest rates can be
expected to lead to higher interest rates applicable to the variable rate investments we may hold and to declines in the value of any fixed rate investments we may hold. However, we expect that many of our variable rate investments provide for an
interest rate floor, which may prevent our interest income from increasing until benchmark interest rates increase beyond a threshold amount. To the extent that a substantial portion of our investments may be in variable rate investments, an
increase in interest rates beyond this threshold would make it easier for us to meet or exceed the hurdle rate applicable to the income incentive fee, and may result in a substantial increase in our net investment income and to the amount of
incentive fees payable to the Adviser with respect to our increased <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-incentive</FONT> fee net investment income. A prolonged reduction in interest rates could reduce our gross investment income and could result in
a decrease in our net investment income if such decreases in interest rates are not offset by a corresponding increase in the spread over the specified reference rate that we earn on any portfolio investments, a decrease in our operating expenses or
a decrease in the interest rate of our floating interest rate liabilities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To the extent that any of our credit facilities or other
financing arrangements that we enter into are based on a floating interest rate, we will be subject to risks relating to changes in market interest rates. In periods of rising interest rates when we have such debt outstanding, or financing
arrangements in effect, our interest expense would increase, which could reduce our net investment income, especially to the extent we hold fixed rate investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expect that our long-term investments will be financed primarily with equity and debt. If deemed prudent, we may use interest rate risk
management techniques in an effort to minimize our exposure to interest rate fluctuations. These techniques may include various interest rate hedging activities to the extent permitted by the 1940 Act. Adverse developments resulting from changes in
interest rates or hedging transactions could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We plan to invest primarily in illiquid debt securities of private companies. Most of our investments will not have a readily available market
price, and we will value these investments at fair value as determined in good faith pursuant </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman; " ALIGN="left"><B>Directors and Executive Officers. </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Board of Directors and Executive Officers </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our business and affairs are managed under the direction of our Board of Directors. The responsibilities of the Board include, among other
things, the oversight of our investment activities, oversight of the Adviser&#8217;s valuation of our assets, oversight of our financing arrangements and corporate governance activities. The Board consists of four Directors, three of whom are not
&#8220;interested persons,&#8221; as defined in the 1940 Act, of the Fund or the Adviser and are &#8220;independent,&#8221; as determined by the Board. We refer to these individuals as our Independent Directors. The Board appoints our executive
officers, who serve at the discretion of the Board. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">123 </P>

have a compensation committee because our executive officers do not receive any direct compensation from us. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Audit Committee </I></B></P>

committee members are Jeff Van Horn (Chair), David Canter, and Seema Chetal. Each of the members of the audit committee meets the independence requirements of Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10A-3</FONT> of the Exchange Act and, in addition,
is not an &#8220;interested person,&#8221; as defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act, of the Fund or of the Adviser. The Board has determined that each of Ms.&nbsp;Chetal and Mr.&nbsp;Van Horn is an &#8220;audit committee financial
expert&#8221; as defined by Item 407 of Regulation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-K</FONT> promulgated under the Exchange Act. The primary functions of the audit committee are to oversee the integrity of the Fund&#8217;s accounting policies,
financial reporting process and system of internal controls regarding finance and accounting policies and to establish guidelines and oversee the investment valuation process followed by the Valuation Designee (the Adviser) and to provide
information to the Board on matters relating to the valuation of the Fund&#8217;s investments. The audit </P>

</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The nominating and corporate governance committee operates pursuant to a charter and consists of three members, including a
chairperson of the nominating and corporate governance committee. The nominating and corporate governance committee members are David Canter (Chair), Seema Chetal and Jeff Van Horn. Each of the members of the nominating and corporate governance
committee is not an &#8220;interested person,&#8221; as defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act, of the Fund or of the Adviser. The primary function of the nominating and corporate governance committee is to consider and make
recommendations to the Board regarding certain governance matters, including selection of Directors for election, selection of Director nominees to fill vacancies on the Board or a committee thereof, development and revision, as appropriate, of
applicable corporate governance documentation and practices and oversight of the evaluation of the Board. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">When nominating Director
candidates, the nominating and corporate governance committee will take into consideration such factors as it deems appropriate in accordance with its charter. Among the qualifications considered in the selection of candidates, the nominating and
corporate governance committee considers the following attributes and criteria of candidates: experience, including experience with investment companies and other organizations of comparable purpose, skills, expertise, diversity, including diversity
of gender, race and national origin, personal and professional integrity, time availability in light of other commitments, conflicts of interest and such other relevant factors that the nominating and corporate governance committee considers
appropriate in the context of the needs of the Board, including, when applicable, to enhance the ability of the Board or committees of the Board to fulfill their duties and/or to satisfy any independence or other applicable requirements imposed by
law, rule, regulation or listing standard. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The nominating and corporate governance committee will consider candidates suggested by its
members and other members of the Board, as well as the Fund&#8217;s management and shareholders. A Fund shareholder who wishes to recommend a prospective nominee for the Board must provide written notice to the Secretary of the Fund in accordance
with the requirements set forth in the Fund&#8217;s bylaws. This notice must contain, as to each nominee, all of the information relating to such person as would be required to be disclosed in a proxy statement meeting the requirements of Regulation
14A under the Exchange Act, and certain other information set forth in the bylaws. In order to be eligible to be a nominee for election as a Director by a shareholder, such potential nominee must deliver to our Corporate Secretary a written
questionnaire providing the requested information about the background and qualifications of such person and a written representation and agreement that such person is not and will not become a party to any voting agreements, any agreement or
understanding with any person with respect to any compensation or indemnification in connection with service on the Board, and would be in compliance with all of our publicly disclosed corporate governance, conflict of interest, confidentiality and
share ownership and trading policies and guidelines. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A copy of the charter of the nominating and corporate governance committee is
available in print to any shareholder who requests it and will also be available via the Fund&#8217;s password-protected investor portal. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Board
Leadership Structure </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our business and affairs are managed under the direction of our Board. Among other things, our Board sets broad
policies for us and approves the appointment of our investment adviser, administrator and officers. The role of our Board, and of any individual Director, is one of oversight and not of management of our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> affairs. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under our charter and bylaws, our Board may designate one of our Directors as chair to
preside over meetings of the Board and meetings of shareholders, and to perform such other duties as may be assigned to him or her by our Board. The Board has appointed Samuel Robinson, who is an &#8220;interested person,&#8221; as defined in
Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act, of the Fund, to serve in the role of chairperson of the Board. The chairperson&#8217;s role is to preside at all meetings of the Board and to act as a liaison with the Adviser, counsel and other Directors
generally between meetings. The Board believes that Mr.&nbsp;Robinson is the Director with the most knowledge of the Fund&#8217;s business strategy and is best situated to serve as chairperson of the Board. We are aware of the potential conflicts
that may arise when a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-Independent</FONT> Director is chairperson of the Board, but believe these potential conflicts are offset by our corporate governance policies, which include regular meetings of the
Independent Directors in executive session without the presence of interested Directors and management, the establishment of two standing committees comprised solely of Independent Directors and the appointment of a chief compliance officer, with
whom the Independent Directors meet regularly without the presence of Interested Directors and other members of management, for administering our compliance policies and procedures. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While the Fund currently does not have a policy mandating a Lead Independent Director, the Board believes that having an Independent Director
fill the lead Director role is appropriate. Seema Chetal has been appointed to serve as Lead Independent Director. The Lead Independent Director, among other things, works with the chairperson of the Board in the preparation of the agenda for each
Board meeting and in determining the need for meetings of the Board, chairs any meeting of the Independent Directors in executive session, facilitates communications between other members of the Board and the chairperson of the Board and/or the
chief executive officer and otherwise consults with the chairperson of the Board and/or the chief executive officer on matters relating to corporate governance and performance of the Board. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board reviews matters related to its leadership structure annually. The Board has determined that its leadership structure is appropriate
because it allows the Board to exercise informed and independent judgment over the matters under its purview and it allocates areas of responsibility among committees of Directors and the full board in a manner that enhances effective oversight.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board believes that its leadership structure is the optimal structure for us at this time. Our Board, which will review its
leadership structure periodically as part of its annual self-assessment process, further believes that its structure is presently appropriate to enable it to exercise its oversight of us. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Board Role in Risk Oversight </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Through its
direct oversight role, and indirectly through its committees, the Board performs a risk oversight function for the Fund consisting of, among other things, the following activities: (1)&nbsp;at regular and special Board meetings, and on an ad hoc
basis as needed, receiving and reviewing reports related to the performance and operations of the Fund; (2)&nbsp;reviewing and approving, as applicable, its compliance policies and procedures; (3)&nbsp;meeting with the portfolio management team to
review investment strategies, techniques and the processes used to manage related risks; (4)&nbsp;overseeing the Fund&#8217;s Valuation Designee (the Adviser) and the investment valuation process via its valuation committee that operates pursuant to
authority assigned to it by the Board; (5)&nbsp;meeting, or reviewing reports prepared by the representatives of key service providers, including the Fund&#8217;s investment adviser, administrator, custodian and independent registered public
accounting firm, to review and discuss the Fund&#8217;s activities and to provide direction with respect thereto; (6)&nbsp;reviewing periodically, and at least annually, the Fund&#8217;s fidelity bond, directors and officers, and errors and
omissions insurance policies and such other insurance policies as may be appropriate; (7)&nbsp;overseeing the Fund&#8217;s accounting and financial reporting processes, including supervision of the Fund&#8217;s independent registered public
accounting firm to ensure that they provide timely analyses of significant financial reporting and internal control issues; and (8)&nbsp;overseeing the services of the Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer to test its compliance procedures and those
of its service providers. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">129 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board also performs its risk oversight responsibilities with the assistance of the
Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer. The Board receives a quarterly report from the Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer, who reports on, among other things, the Fund&#8217;s compliance with applicable securities laws and its internal compliance
policies and procedures. In addition, the Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer prepares a written report annually evaluating, among other things, the adequacy and effectiveness of the compliance policies and procedures of the Fund and certain of
its service providers. The Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer&#8217;s report, which is reviewed by the Board, addresses at a minimum: (1)&nbsp;the operation and effectiveness of the compliance policies and procedures of the Fund and certain of
its service providers since the last report; (2)&nbsp;any material changes to such policies and procedures since the last report; (3)&nbsp;any recommendations for changes to such policies and procedures as a result of the Fund&#8217;s chief
compliance officer&#8217;s annual review; and (4)&nbsp;any material compliance matters that have occurred since the date of the last report about which the Board would reasonably need to know to oversee the Fund&#8217;s compliance activities and
risks. The Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer also meets separately in executive session with the Independent Directors at least once each year. In addition to compliance reports from the Fund&#8217;s chief compliance officer, the Board also
receives reports and updates from legal counsel to the Fund regarding legal, regulatory and governance matters. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Oversight of our
investment activities extends to oversight of the risk management processes employed by the Adviser as part of its <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> management of our investment activities.
The Board anticipates reviewing risk management processes at both regular and special board meetings throughout the year, consulting with appropriate representatives of the Adviser as necessary and periodically requesting the production of risk
management reports or presentations. The goal of the Board&#8217;s risk oversight function is to ensure that the risks associated with our investment activities are accurately identified, thoroughly investigated and responsibly addressed. Investors
should note, however, that the Board&#8217;s oversight function cannot eliminate all risks or ensure that particular events do not adversely affect the value of investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We believe that the role of our Board in risk oversight is effective and appropriate given the extensive regulation to which we are already
subject and to which we will be subject as a BDC. As a BDC, we will be required to comply with certain regulatory requirements that control the levels of risk in our business and operations. For example, we are and will be limited in our ability to
enter into transactions with our affiliates, including investing in any portfolio company in which one of our affiliates currently has an investment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Portfolio Management </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I></I></B><B><I></I></B>The Adviser, Sagard Holdings Manager (US) LLC, serves as our investment adviser pursuant to the Advisory Agreement.
The Adviser is registered as an investment adviser under the Advisers Act. Subject to the overall supervision of our Board, the Adviser is responsible for evaluating and monitoring our investments and providing day-to-day managerial and
administrative services to the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I></I></B><B><I></I></B>Our primary portfolio manager, Dev Gopalan, is primarily responsible for
the day-to-day management of our portfolio, with oversight and approval by the Investment Committee. To the extent that we make opportunistic credit investments, Mustafa Humayun will act as portfolio manager for those investments (together with Dev
Gopalan, the &#8220;Portfolio Managers&#8221;) and will also be responsible for the day-to-day management of that portion of the portfolio, with oversight and approval from the Investment Committee. Each Portfolio Manager is a member of the
Investment Committee. The Portfolio Managers and members of the Investment Committee also manage other private funds/investment companies, other pooled investment vehicles and other accounts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">New investment opportunities and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">follow-on</FONT> investments in existing portfolio companies require
majority approval of the eligible voting members of the Investment Committee. The Investment Committee will meet regularly to consider our investments, direct our strategic initiatives and supervise the actions taken by the Adviser on our behalf. In
addition, the Investment Committee reviews and determines whether to make prospective investments identified by the Adviser and monitors the performance of our investment portfolio, while the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> management of investments approved by the Investment Committee is overseen primarily by the Portfolio Managers. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Director Independence </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While we are not
listed on any public securities exchange, we intend to comply with listing standards of the New York Stock Exchange (&#8220;<U>NYSE</U>&#8221;) requiring listed companies to have a board of directors with at least a majority of independent
directors. The NYSE listing standards provide that a director of a BDC will be considered to be independent if he or she is not an &#8220;interested person&#8221; of the Fund, as defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Based on these standards, the Board has determined that David Canter, Seema Chetal, and Jeff Van Horn are independent (or not
&#8220;interested persons&#8221; of the Fund). Based upon information requested from each such Director concerning his or her background, employment and affiliations, the Board has affirmatively determined that none of the Independent Directors has
a material business or professional relationship with the Fund, other than in his or her capacity as a member of the Board or any committee thereof. All of the members of the Audit Committee and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee are not
&#8220;interested persons&#8221; as defined in Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Certain Relationships and Related Transactions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund is subject to certain actual and potential conflicts of interest arising from the relationships among the Fund, the Adviser, Sagard,
SHI, PCC and their respective affiliates. These conflicts arise, among other circumstances, in connection with the Adviser&#8217;s simultaneous management of Other Sagard Clients (as defined below), the fee and compensation arrangements between the
Fund and the Adviser, the role of SHI as the Fund&#8217;s initial majority shareholder (directly and indirectly through its wholly-owned subsidiary), and the Adviser&#8217;s role as both investment adviser and administrator to the Fund. You should
be aware that individual conflicts will not necessarily be resolved in favor of the Fund&#8217;s shareholders. The following description of conflicts is not exhaustive, and additional and different conflicts may arise as the Fund&#8217;s investment
program develops. Although the various conflicts discussed herein are generally described separately, prospective investors should consider the potential effects of the interplay of multiple conflicts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The members of the senior management and investment teams of the Adviser serve or may serve as officers, directors or principals of entities
that operate in the same or a related line of business as the Fund, or of investment vehicles managed by the same personnel. For example, the Adviser is the investment adviser or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> adviser to
multiple other Sagard-affiliated funds and investment vehicles (collectively, &#8220;<U>Other</U> <U>Sagard Clients</U>&#8221;), and the officers, managers and other personnel of the Adviser may serve in similar or other capacities for the
investment advisers to future investment vehicles affiliated with Sagard. In the future, these persons and other affiliates of Sagard may organize other debt-related programs and acquire for their own account debt-related investments that may be
suitable for the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In serving in these multiple and other capacities, the Adviser&#8217;s personnel may have obligations to investors
in Other Sagard Clients, the fulfillment of which may not be in the Fund&#8217;s best interests or in the best interests of the Fund&#8217;s shareholders. The Fund&#8217;s investment objectives may overlap with the investment objectives of such
investment funds, accounts or other investment vehicles. As a result, the Adviser and its affiliates may face conflicts of interest in allocating investment opportunities among the Fund and the Other Sagard Clients, and there can be no assurance
that the Fund will receive its proportionate share of any particular investment opportunity. Any actions taken by the Adviser in its capacity as adviser to an Other Sagard Client that are more favorable to such Other Sagard Client may, in certain
circumstances, be adverse to the interests of the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Investment Advisory Agreement and Administration Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Advisory Agreement, the Adviser will provide us with investment advisory services for which we will pay the Adviser a
management fee, quarterly in arrears, at an annual rate of 1.25% of the average monthly value of the Fund&#8217;s net assets (subject to the Advisory Fee Waiver Period, during which the effective rate is 0.85% per annum) as well as an incentive fee
based on performance. See &#8220;<I>Item 1. Business&nbsp;&#8212; Management Agreements</I>&#8221; for a description of how the fees payable to the Adviser are determined. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The incentive fee will be computed and paid on income that we may not have yet received in cash. This fee structure may create an incentive
for our Adviser to invest in certain types of securities that may have a high degree of risk. We will rely on input from investment professionals from our Adviser to value our portfolio investments. Our Adviser&#8217;s base management fee and
incentive fee will be based on the value of our investments, and there may be a conflict of interest when personnel of our Adviser assist in determining periodic fair values for our portfolio investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Administration Agreement, the Adviser will also oversee our
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> operations, including the provision of general ledger accounting, fund accounting, legal services, investor relations, certain government and regulatory
affairs activities, and other administrative services. There is no separate fee paid by us to the Adviser in connection with the administrative services provided under the Administration Agreement, provided, however, that we reimburse the Adviser
for all costs and expenses incurred by the Adviser in performing its obligations and providing personnel and facilities thereunder. See &#8220;<I>Item 1. Business&nbsp;&#8212; Management Agreements</I>&#8221; for a description of our obligation to
reimburse the Adviser under the Administration Agreement. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Expense Support Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have entered into the Expense Support Agreement with the Adviser, pursuant to which the Adviser (1)&nbsp;has agreed to advance or otherwise
bear all of our organization and offering expenses through December&nbsp;31, 2026 and (2) may elect, in its discretion, to make Expense Payments on our behalf, provided that no portion of any Expense Payment will be used to pay any interest expense
or distribution and/or shareholder servicing fees of the Fund. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Expense Support Agreement, in no event will the Fund bear organization and offering expenses in excess of the $1.5 million O&amp;O Cap; to
the extent such expenses exceed the O&amp;O Cap, the Adviser will pay the excess on the Fund&#8217;s behalf without reimbursement or recoupment. The Fund&#8217;s right to receive an Expense Payment becomes an asset of the Fund once the Adviser
commits in writing to pay it. Any Expense Payment that the Adviser has committed to pay must be paid by the Adviser to or on behalf of the Fund in any combination of cash or other immediately available funds no later than 45 days after such
commitment was made in writing, and/or offset against amounts due from us to the Adviser or its affiliates. Beginning after December 31, 2026, the Adviser will be entitled to reimbursement of Expense Payments from us if Available Operating Funds
exceed the cumulative distributions accrued to the Fund&#8217;s shareholders, among other conditions. See &#8220;<I>Item&nbsp;1.</I> <I>Business&nbsp;&#8212; Management Agreements&nbsp;&#8212; Expense Support and Conditional</I> <I>Reimbursement
</I><I>Agreement.</I>&#8221; for additional information regarding the Expense Support Agreement. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Allocation of the Adviser&#8217;s Time </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund relies on the Adviser to manage the Fund&#8217;s
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> activities and to implement its investment strategies. The Adviser and Sagard and certain of their affiliates are presently, and plan in the future to
continue to be, involved with activities that are unrelated to the Fund. As a result of these activities, the Adviser and Sagard and certain of their affiliates will have conflicts of interest in allocating their time between the Fund and other
activities in which they are or may become involved, including the Adviser&#8217;s existing and future advisory relationships with Other Sagard Clients. The Adviser and Sagard and their employees will devote only as much of their time to the
Fund&#8217;s business as the Adviser and Sagard, in their judgment, determine is reasonably required, which may be substantially less than their full time. Therefore, the Adviser, its personnel and certain affiliates may experience conflicts of
interest in allocating management time, services and functions among the Fund and any other business ventures in which they or any of their key personnel, as applicable, are or may become involved. This could result in actions that are more
favorable to Other Sagard Clients or other affiliated entities than to the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">However, the Fund believes that the members of the
Adviser&#8217;s management and the other key debt finance professionals have sufficient time to fully discharge their responsibilities to the Fund and to the other businesses in which they are involved. The Fund believes that its affiliates and
executive officers will devote the time required to manage the Fund&#8217;s business and expect that the amount of time a particular executive officer or affiliate devotes to the Fund will vary during the course of the year and depend on the
Fund&#8217;s business activities at the given time. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Competition and Allocation of Investment Opportunities </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a BDC regulated under the 1940 Act, the Fund is subject to certain restrictions on affiliated
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> transactions. Sections 17(d) and 57(a)(4) of the 1940 Act and Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">17d-1</FONT> promulgated thereunder generally prohibit BDCs from participating in joint
transactions, including <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investments,</FONT> with certain affiliates of the BDC without prior SEC approval, in the absence of an exemptive order. These restrictions apply to transactions originated by the BDC or
its affiliates, and extend to transactions in which price is not the only negotiated term. As a result, without the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order, the Fund&#8217;s ability to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-invest</FONT> alongside Other Sagard Accounts in negotiated private credit transactions is significantly limited. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We, the Adviser and certain of our affiliates have filed an application with the SEC for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order under Sections 17(d) and 57(i) of the 1940 Act and Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">17d-1</FONT> thereunder, to allow certain
</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">134 </P>

managed funds and investment vehicles, each of whose investment adviser is the Adviser or an investment adviser controlling, controlled by or under common control with the Adviser (and including
any direct or indirect, wholly- or majority-owned subsidiary of the Adviser or its affiliates), to participate in negotiated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> transactions where doing so is consistent with regulatory requirements
and other pertinent factors, and pursuant to the conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order. If granted, the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order will permit us, subject

conflicts of interest may also arise in determining which investment opportunities should be presented to the Fund versus Other Accounts, including as a result of the different fee and compensation structures applicable to the Fund and Other
Accounts. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To mitigate allocation conflicts, the Adviser has established an allocation policy designed to ensure that investment
opportunities are allocated among the Fund and Other Sagard Accounts in a manner that is fair and equitable over time. In allocating investment opportunities among eligible vehicles, the Adviser will consider a range of factors, which may include,
among others: the Fund&#8217;s and Other Sagard Accounts&#8217; investment objectives, policies, restrictions and guidelines (including term, investment period, and geographic, diversification and concentration restrictions); the amount of capital
required to fund the investment opportunity and current and projected available capital and borrowing capacity; undrawn capital available for investment; transaction sourcing; targeted rate of return and investment holding period; the ability to
accommodate structural, timing and other aspects of the investment opportunity; timing necessary to execute the investment; existing portfolio construction and diversification; the size, liquidity and duration of the investment opportunity; stage of
development of the prospective portfolio company and anticipated holding period; portfolio composition and concentration parameters (including geography, industry, issuer, volatility and leverage); suitability as a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">follow-on</FONT> investment for an existing portfolio company; use of leverage in the proposed capital structure; availability of other suitable investments; supply and demand for the investment opportunity at a
given price level; risk considerations; industry and other allocation targets; minimum and maximum investment size requirements; tax and accounting implications; current and anticipated market conditions; potential conflicts of interest arising from
more than one Fund or Other Sagard Account pursuing the same opportunity; any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;ramp-up&#8221;</FONT> period; any priority obligations to offer opportunities; related investments; any tax, legal or regulatory
restrictions deemed relevant by the Adviser; any other factors described in the Adviser&#8217;s allocation policy or Form ADV; any other relevant limitations in the governing documents of the Fund or Other Sagard Accounts; and any other factors
deemed relevant by the Adviser in the exercise of its judgment. Allocation determinations are inherently subjective and give rise to conflicts of interest because the Adviser may have an incentive to allocate investment opportunities to the vehicle
from which it or its affiliates derive greater fees or other economic benefits, and because principals and employees of the Adviser may hold interests in the Fund or Other Sagard Accounts that create additional incentives. There can be no assurance
that the Fund&#8217;s actual allocation of an investment opportunity, if any, or the terms on which that allocation is made will be as favorable as they would be if the conflicts of interest described herein did not exist. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Portions of any investment opportunity not allocated to the Fund or Other Sagard Accounts
may be offered as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> opportunities to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investors,</FONT> strategic partners or others in the Adviser&#8217;s discretion. In addition, the Adviser and its
affiliates from time to time provide certain investors in Other Sagard Accounts or third parties with contractual rights to participate in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> opportunities alongside the Fund, and there will be
times where a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investor</FONT> or Other Sagard Account will invest alongside the Fund in the same transaction or, where the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investor</FONT> or Other Sagard Account holds priority
or other contractual <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> rights, will receive an allocation of an investment opportunity ahead of, or to the exclusion of, an allocation to the Fund, subject in each case to the 1940 Act, the
conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order (once obtained) and the Adviser&#8217;s allocation policy. This could result in the Fund not participating in an investment opportunity at all or participating
to a lesser extent than it otherwise would have. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sagard has expanded, and may continue to expand, its investment management services
beyond the Fund, including through additional <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">closed-end</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">open-end</FONT> funds, separately managed accounts, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> vehicles,
special purpose vehicles and other investment vehicles (which may constitute additional Other Accounts), which could give rise to additional conflicts of interest not specifically described herein. Further, Sagard plans to continue to invest capital
of third parties and its affiliates in a wide variety of credit investment opportunities, which may include investment vehicles that have investment strategies or objectives that overlap with the Fund&#8217;s strategy. It is expected that the
activities of Other Accounts may compete with the Fund for investment opportunities consistent with the Fund&#8217;s investment objectives, and in such circumstances, the Adviser expects to allocate such opportunities in a manner consistent with the
1940 Act, the conditions of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order (once obtained) and the Adviser&#8217;s allocation policy. There can be no assurance that the Fund will ultimately be allocated all opportunities
that are consistent with its investment objectives, or that the allocation process will be free of the conflicts of interest described above. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Conflicts Relating to SHI and PCC </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SHI, a
subsidiary of PCC, is the Fund&#8217;s initial majority shareholder (directly and indirectly through SHI&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiary), having made the Seed Investment and having received Common Shares in connection with the SPV Contribution.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SHI&#8217;s position as a significant shareholder creates potential conflicts of interest. For example, SHI may have interests in the
Fund&#8217;s investment performance, valuation and distribution policy that are different from the interests of unaffiliated shareholders. The Adviser, which is indirectly owned by Sagard, may be influenced, directly or indirectly, by SHI&#8217;s or
PCC&#8217;s interests as controlling shareholder of Sagard in a manner that is adverse to unaffiliated shareholders, even though neither SHI nor PCC has a contractual right to direct the Fund&#8217;s investment decisions. Conversely, the Adviser may
have an incentive to favor the Fund&#8217;s short-term performance during the period in which SHI, directly or indirectly, is the majority shareholder (which could be at the expense of Other Sagard Clients) in order to facilitate the reduction of
SHI&#8217;s ownership percentage by attracting new investors. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the Initial Portfolio was originated and managed by investment
personnel of the Adviser prior to the BDC Election Date, and the SPV Contribution involved the transfer of the Initial Portfolio from SHI&#8217;s affiliated vehicle to the Fund prior to the Fund&#8217;s election to be regulated as a BDC. The
valuation of the Initial Portfolio at the time of the SPV Contribution was determined by the Adviser in consultation with an independent third-party valuation firm engaged by the Adviser and may present a conflict of interest, as the Adviser has an
incentive to value the Initial Portfolio at a level that is favorable to SHI (the wholly-owned subsidiary of which received Common Shares in exchange for the SPV Contribution at a price per share based on the then-current NAV). Although the Board
supervised the valuation process, there can be no assurance that the valuation used in connection with the SPV Contribution fully reflected the fair market value of the Initial Portfolio. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Advisory Fee Structure </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Income Incentive Fee is calculated quarterly based on the Fund&#8217;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net
Investment Income, subject to the Hurdle Rate. This fee structure may incentivize the Adviser to favor investments that maximize short-term current income (which increases the Income Incentive Fee) over investments that may be more appropriate for
the Fund&#8217;s long-term performance or capital preservation objectives. The Adviser may also be incentivized to use leverage to increase income available for distribution and thereby increase the Income Incentive Fee, which may increase the risk
of loss of principal. The Capital Gains Incentive Fee, which is calculated on a cumulative realized net gain basis, may incentivize the Adviser to selectively realize gains or to hold investments longer than appropriate in order to manage cumulative
capital gain calculations. In addition, the Adviser has an incentive to recommend the use of leverage or the issuance of additional equity to increase the average monthly value of net assets, which forms the basis for the Base Management Fee. These
incentives may cause the Adviser to make riskier or more speculative investments or to rely more heavily on leverage than would otherwise be the case, which could result in higher investment losses, particularly during cyclical economic downturns.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Valuation Conflicts </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value
of most of the Fund&#8217;s investments will not be readily determinable because there is no active trading market for them. The Adviser, as the Board-designated valuation designee under Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">2a-5</FONT> of the 1940
Act, is responsible for implementing the valuation process for the Fund&#8217;s portfolio investments. The Adviser has a direct financial interest in the valuation of the Fund&#8217;s investments because: (i)&nbsp;the Base Management Fee is
calculated based on the Fund&#8217;s net assets, which reflects the fair value of the Fund&#8217;s portfolio investments; and (ii)&nbsp;the Capital Gains Incentive Fee is based on cumulative net realized capital gains, which includes unrealized
depreciation as an offset. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This creates a conflict of interest in that the Adviser may have an incentive to ascribe higher fair values to
the Fund&#8217;s investments in order to increase the Base Management Fee base. Although the Adviser is required to engage independent third-party pricing and valuation services and to report quarterly to the Board&#8217;s audit committee, and the
Board remains ultimately responsible for the fair valuation of the Fund&#8217;s portfolio investments, there can be no assurance that the valuation process will be free of bias resulting from this conflict. The exercise of discretion in valuation
may also give rise to conflicts in connection with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investments</FONT> alongside Other Sagard Clients, where the Adviser simultaneously determines the fair value of the same portfolio company or investment for
multiple funds. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Material <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Public</FONT> Information </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Adviser and its affiliates may from time to time come into possession of material, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-public</FONT>
information (&#8220;<U>MNPI</U>&#8221;) about issuers whose securities may be held or considered for purchase or sale by the Fund. The receipt of MNPI may restrict the Fund&#8217;s ability to buy or sell securities issued by such companies. As a
result, the Fund may not be able to initiate a transaction that it otherwise might have initiated, or sell an investment that it otherwise might have sold, due to these restrictions. In addition, personnel of the Adviser or its affiliates who serve
on the boards of directors of portfolio companies as a result of the Fund&#8217;s investments may acquire MNPI in the course of their board service. Although the Adviser maintains information barrier procedures and a Code of Ethics designed to
manage the flow of MNPI, there can be no assurance that such procedures will be effective in all circumstances or that the Fund will not be restricted from taking actions that would otherwise be in its best interest. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Personnel of the Adviser or its affiliates may serve as directors or observers on the boards of directors of portfolio companies. While
conflicts of interest may arise to the extent that the fiduciary duties of such a director to a portfolio company conflict with the fiduciary duties owed to the Fund, it is expected that, in many cases, the interests of the portfolio company and the
Fund will be aligned. However, where the Adviser or its affiliates hold investments in multiple portfolio companies that may be competitors or counterparties to each other, director-level conflicts may arise that cannot be resolved in a manner
favorable to all parties. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Board Oversight and Regulatory Protections </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a BDC regulated under the 1940 Act, the Fund expects to benefit from several regulatory protections intended to mitigate conflicts of
interest that are not available to investors in private investment vehicles such as the Other Sagard Clients. The Board, a majority of which must comprise persons who are not &#8220;interested persons&#8221; of the Fund as defined in
Section&nbsp;2(a)(19) of the 1940 Act, is responsible for overseeing the management and operations of the Fund, including reviewing and approving the Advisory Agreement and Administration Agreement on an annual basis (following their initial terms),
reviewing the fees paid to the Adviser, and overseeing the valuation process. Certain transactions between the Fund and affiliates of the Adviser, including transactions that may create the conflicts of interest described above, are subject to the
restrictions under Sections&nbsp;17 and 57 of the 1940 Act, which may require Board approval or SEC approval, as applicable. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In
connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Co-Investment</FONT> Exemptive Order, the &#8220;required majority&#8221; of the Board (a majority of Directors who are not interested persons and who have no financial interest in any <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> transaction) must approve certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-investment</FONT> transactions in which price is not the only negotiated term. These board-level protections are designed to
protect the Fund&#8217;s shareholders from conflicts inherent in affiliated transactions, but investors should not rely solely on Board oversight to protect their interests in all circumstances. In some cases, conflicts may not be effectively
mitigated by Board oversight, particularly where conflicts are structural (such as the Adviser&#8217;s incentive to maximize fee income) or arise in connection with Adviser discretion that is not subject to individual Board approval. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Distribution of Common Shares </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The
Adviser or its affiliates may pay compensation, out of their own funds and not as an additional charge to the Fund or investors, to selected brokers, dealers or other financial intermediaries, including affiliated broker dealers, in connection with
the distribution of Common Shares and/or for the purpose of introducing a selling agent to the Fund, promoting the recommendation of an investment in the Common Shares or in connection with providing services intended to result in the sale of Common
Shares and/or shareholder support services, and such payment amounts may be significant. This compensation may differ among the recipients in amount or in the amount of calculation. Such compensation may take various forms, including a fixed fee, a
fee determined by a formula that takes into account the amount of client assets invested, the timing of investment or the overall NAV of the Fund or a class of Common Shares, or a fee determined in some other method by negotiation between the
Adviser and such financial intermediaries or service providers. The receipt of the additional compensation by a selling agent or financial intermediary may create potential conflicts of interest between an investor and its broker or dealer or other
financial intermediary who is recommending the Common Shares over other potential investments. Financial intermediaries may also charge investors, at the financial intermediaries&#8217; discretion, a placement fee based on the purchase price of
Common Shares purchased by the investor. As a result of the various payments that financial intermediaries may receive from investors and the Adviser, the amount of compensation that a financial intermediary may receive in connection with the sale
of Common Shares may be greater than the compensation it may receive for the distribution of other investment products. This difference in compensation may create an incentive for a financial intermediary to recommend the Fund over another
investment product. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While the Adviser or its affiliates have and may continue to pay compensation to such entities in connection with the
offering of Common Shares, it is under no obligation to pay such fees and may decide not to do so in the future to the extent that any such compensation is permitted to be borne by the Fund. In return for this compensation, the Adviser and its
affiliates expect to receive certain marketing or servicing advantages that are not generally available to funds that do not make such payments. Such advantages are expected to include, without limitation, placement of the Fund on a list of funds
offered as investment options to the intermediary&#8217;s or service provider&#8217;s clients (sometimes referred to as &#8220;shelf space&#8221;); access to the intermediary&#8217;s registered representatives; and/or ability to assist in training
and educating the intermediary&#8217;s registered representatives. In addition, as a result of such additional compensation </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Distribution Reinvestment Plan </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have
adopted a distribution reinvestment plan with respect to our Common Shares, pursuant to which we will reinvest all cash dividends declared by the Board on behalf of holders of our Common Shares who do not elect to receive their dividends in cash as
provided below. As a result, if the Board authorizes, and we declare, a cash dividend or other distribution on our Common Shares, then our shareholders who have not opted out of our distribution reinvestment plan will have their cash distributions
automatically reinvested in additional Common Shares as described below, rather than receiving the cash dividend or other distribution. Distributions on fractional shares will be credited to each participating shareholder&#8217;s account to three
decimal places. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">No action is required on the part of a registered holder of our Common Shares to have his, her or its cash dividend or
other distribution reinvested in our shares. Unless a shareholder specifically elects to receive cash, all distributions will be automatically reinvested in additional Common Shares. Shareholders who wish to receive distributions in cash instead of
having them reinvested may elect to &#8220;opt out&#8221; of the Fund&#8217;s distribution reinvestment plan in their subscription agreements or by subsequently notifying the Plan Administrator in writing in accordance with the terms below (other
than clients of certain participating brokers that do not permit automatic enrollment in our distribution reinvestment plan). Clients of certain participating brokers that do not permit automatic enrollment in our distribution reinvestment plan will
automatically receive their distributions in cash unless they elect to have their cash distributions reinvested in additional Common Shares. </P>

Administrator may hold Common Shares acquired under the distribution reinvestment plan in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-certificated</FONT> form in its name or that of its nominee, and will not issue share certificates to participants. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A shareholder may elect to receive distributions in cash or terminate his, her or its
account under the distribution reinvestment plan by so notifying the Plan Administrator in writing no later than 10 calendar days prior to the record date for an applicable distribution; otherwise, such election or termination shall be effective
only with respect to any subsequent distributions. Such election shall remain in effect until the shareholder notifies the Plan Administrator in writing of its withdrawal, which withdrawal will be effective immediately if notice is received no later
than 10 calendar days prior to the record date for the next distribution; otherwise, such withdrawal will be effective only with respect to any subsequent distributions. If a participant elects to tender its Common Shares in full in connection with
any tender offer by the Fund, any Common Shares issued to the participant under the distribution reinvestment plan subsequent to the expiration of the relevant tender offer will be considered part of the participant&#8217;s prior tender, and the
participant&#8217;s participation in the distribution reinvestment plan will be terminated as of the valuation date of the applicable tender offer. Any distributions to be paid to such shareholder on or after such date will be paid in cash on the
scheduled distribution payment date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you elect to opt out of the distribution reinvestment plan in accordance with its terms, you will

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The price for Common Shares acquired under our distribution reinvestment plan will be equal to the most recent available NAV per share for
such shares at the time the distribution is payable, subject to adjustment to the extent required by Section&nbsp;23 of the 1940 Act. Shareholders will not pay upfront selling commissions when purchasing shares under our distribution reinvestment
plan; however, all shares, including those purchased under our distribution reinvestment plan, will be subject to any ongoing shareholder servicing and/or distribution fees. Common Shares issued pursuant to our distribution reinvestment plan will
have the same voting rights as the Common Shares offered in the Private Offering. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund may terminate the distribution reinvestment
plan upon written notice at least 10 business days prior to any record date for the payment of any distribution. The terms of the distribution reinvestment plan may also be amended or supplemented by the Fund at any time, except that, other than as
necessary or appropriate to comply with applicable law or the rules, regulations or policies of the SEC or any other regulatory authority, any such amendment or supplement will only be effective upon at least 10 business days&#8217; prior written
notice. An amendment or supplement will be deemed accepted by each shareholder unless, prior to its effective date, the Plan Administrator receives written notice of that shareholder&#8217;s termination of participation in the distribution
reinvestment plan. Upon any termination, the Plan Administrator will cause the Common Shares held for each participant under the distribution reinvestment plan to be delivered to the participant. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>General </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our authorized stock consists of

issuance under any equity compensation plans. Under Maryland law, our shareholders generally are not personally liable for our debts or obligations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter provides that a majority of our Board, without any action by shareholders, may amend the charter from time to time to increase or
decrease the aggregate number of shares of stock or the number of shares of stock of any class or series that we have authority to issue. If shares of one class or series of stock are classified or reclassified into shares of another class or series
of stock pursuant to our charter, the number of authorized shares of the former class or series will be automatically decreased and the number of shares of the latter class or series will be automatically increased, in each case by the number of
shares so classified or reclassified, so that the aggregate number of shares of stock of all classes and series that we have authority to issue will not be more than 500,000,000 shares in total. </P>

of holders of our preferred stock, if any preferred stock is outstanding at such time. Subject to the rights of holders of any other class or series of shares, each Common Share is entitled to one vote on all matters submitted to a vote of
shareholders, including the election of directors, and will vote as a single class. Except as may be provided by the Board in setting the terms of classified or reclassified shares, and subject to the express terms of any class or series of
preferred shares, the holders of our Common Shares will possess exclusive voting power. There is no cumulative voting in the election of directors. </P>

distribution fees, shareholder services fees and any other class expenses that may be attributable to the different classes of shares of our Common Shares, following receipt of the Multi-Class Exemptive Relief, if any, the net income attributable

particular class of shares, will be borne on a pro rata basis by each outstanding share of that class. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Limitation on Liability of Directors and
Officers; Indemnification and Advancement of Expenses </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter contains a provision which eliminates directors&#8217; and
officers&#8217; liability to the Fund or our shareholders for money damages to the maximum extent permitted by Maryland law, subject to the requirements of the 1940 Act. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Maryland law requires a Maryland corporation (unless its charter provides otherwise, which our charter does not) to indemnify a director or
officer who has been successful in the defense of any proceeding to which he or she is made, or threatened to be made, a party by reason of his or her service in that capacity. Maryland law permits a Maryland corporation to include in its charter a
provision indemnifying any director or officer made a party to a proceeding by reason of his or her service in such capacity until such time as it is &#8220;established&#8221; that (i)&nbsp;the act or omission of the director or officer was
committed in bad faith or was the result of active and deliberate dishonesty and was material to the matter giving rise to the proceeding; (ii)&nbsp;the individual actually received an improper personal benefit in money, property, or services; or
(iii)&nbsp;in the case of any criminal proceeding, the individual had reasonable cause to believe that the act or omission was unlawful. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">However, under Maryland law, a Maryland corporation may not indemnify for an adverse judgment in a suit by or in the right of the corporation
or for a judgment of liability on the basis that a personal benefit was improperly received unless, in either case, a court orders indemnification, and then only for expenses. In addition, Maryland law permits a corporation to advance reasonable
expenses to a director or officer in advance of final disposition of a proceeding upon the corporation&#8217;s receipt of (a)&nbsp;a written affirmation by the director or officer of his or her good faith belief that he or she has met the standard
of conduct necessary for indemnification by the corporation and (b)&nbsp;a written undertaking by him or her or on his or her behalf to repay the amount paid or reimbursed by the corporation if it is ultimately determined that the standard of
conduct was not met. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter requires us, to the maximum extent permitted by Maryland law and subject to the requirements of the 1940
Act, to indemnify and pay or reimburse reasonable expenses in advance of final disposition of a proceeding to (a)&nbsp;any individual who is a present or former director or officer of the Fund or (b)&nbsp;any individual who, while a director or
officer of the Fund and at the request of the Fund, serves or has served as a director, officer, partner or trustee of another corporation, real estate investment trust, partnership, joint venture, trust, employee benefit plan or any other
enterprise from and against any claim or liability to which such person may become subject or which such person may incur by reason of his or her status as a present or former director or </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">143 </P>

directors and executive officers the maximum indemnification permitted under the MGCL and the 1940 Act. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Maryland Law and Certain Charter Provisions
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Organization and Purpose </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We were formed as a Delaware statutory trust on March&nbsp;20, 2026 and converted to a Maryland corporation effective on September 18, 2026. We
will remain in existence until dissolved in accordance with our charter or pursuant to Maryland law. Under the charter, the Fund is permitted to engage in any lawful act or activity for which corporations may be organized under the general laws of
the State of Maryland, including engaging in business as a business development company under the 1940 Act. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Maryland Anti-takeover Law </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The MGCL and our charter and bylaws contain provisions that could make it more difficult for a potential acquirer to acquire us by means of a
tender offer, proxy contest or otherwise, the material ones of which are discussed below. These provisions are expected to discourage certain coercive takeover practices and inadequate takeover bids and to encourage persons seeking to acquire
control of us to negotiate first with our Board. We expect the benefits of these provisions to outweigh the potential disadvantages of discouraging any such acquisition proposals because, among other things, the negotiation of such proposals may
improve their terms. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Number of Directors; Term and Election; Vacancies; Removal </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter and bylaws provide that the number of directors will be set only by the Board. Our bylaws provide that a majority of our entire
Board may at any time increase or decrease the number of directors. However, the number of directors may never be less than the minimum number required by the MGCL nor, unless our bylaws are amended, more than nine. We have elected to be subject to
the provision of Subtitle 8 of Title 3 of the MGCL regarding the filling of vacancies on the Board. Accordingly, except as may be provided by our Board in setting the terms of any class or series of stock, any and all vacancies on the Board,
including a vacancy resulting from an enlargement of the Board, may be filled only by the affirmative vote of a majority of </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">144 </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
the remaining directors in office, even if the remaining directors do not constitute a quorum, and any director elected to fill a vacancy will serve for the remainder of the full term of the
directorship in which the vacancy occurred and until a successor is elected and qualifies, subject to any applicable requirements of the 1940 Act. Our charter provides that a director may be removed only for cause, as defined in our charter, and
then only by the affirmative vote of at least <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-thirds</FONT> of the votes entitled to be cast in the election of directors. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under the charter, on the date on which the Fund holds its first annual meeting of shareholders, the Board will be divided into three classes,
as nearly equal in number as possible, with the term of one class expiring at each successive annual meeting of shareholders, and each director will hold office for a term expiring at the annual meeting held in the third year following the year of
election and until a successor is elected and qualifies. The Fund is not required to hold an annual meeting in any year in which the election of directors is not required to be acted upon under the 1940 Act; if the Fund does not hold an annual
meeting in a given year, the term of each class of directors is extended for an additional year so that only the term of a single class expires in the year the Fund holds an annual meeting. This provision could delay for up to two years the
replacement of a majority of the Board. Our bylaws provide that the affirmative vote of the holders of a plurality of all votes cast at a meeting of shareholders duly called, and at which a quorum is present, will be required to elect a director.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Action by Shareholders </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under
the MGCL, shareholder action can generally be taken only at an annual or special meeting of shareholders or by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, unless the charter provides for shareholder action by less than unanimous written consent.
Our charter permits shareholder action by less than unanimous written consent to the extent provided in our bylaws, and our bylaws permit shareholders to take action by written consent of holders entitled to cast not less than the minimum number of
votes that would be necessary to authorize or take the action at a meeting of shareholders at which all shareholders entitled to vote on the action were present and voted. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Quorum </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter and bylaws
provide that the presence in person or by proxy of shareholders entitled to cast <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-third</FONT> of the votes entitled to be cast (without regard to class) constitutes a quorum at any meeting of shareholders, except
that, with respect to any matter that under applicable statutes, regulatory requirements or our charter requires approval by a separate vote of one or more classes or series of stock, the presence in person or by proxy of holders of shares entitled
to cast a majority of the votes entitled to be cast by such class or series on that matter is required to constitute a quorum for purposes of that matter. To the extent permitted by Maryland law, this quorum requirement may be changed by our bylaws.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Advance Notice Provisions for Shareholder Nominations and Shareholder Proposals </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our bylaws provide that with respect to any annual meeting of shareholders, nominations of persons for election to the Board and the proposal
of business to be considered by shareholders may be made only (1)&nbsp;pursuant to the Fund&#8217;s notice of meeting, (2)&nbsp;by or at the direction of the Board or (3)&nbsp;by any shareholder of the Fund who was a shareholder of record both at
the time of giving of notice under the bylaws and at the time of the annual meeting, who is entitled to vote at the meeting in the election of each individual so nominated or on any such other business and who has complied with the advance notice
provisions and informational requirements of the bylaws. With respect to special meetings of shareholders, only the business specified in our notice of the meeting may be brought before the meeting. Nominations of persons for election to the Board
at a special meeting may be made only (1)&nbsp;pursuant to the Fund&#8217;s notice of meeting, (2)&nbsp;by or at the direction of the Board or (3)&nbsp;provided that the special meeting has been called in accordance with our bylaws for the purposes
of electing directors, by a shareholder who was a shareholder of record at the time of provision of notice under the bylaws, at the record date set by the Board for purposes of the meeting and at the time of the meeting, who is entitled to vote at
the meeting and who has complied with the advance notice provisions and informational requirements of the bylaws. </P>
