 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The purpose of requiring shareholders to give us advance notice of nominations and other
business is to afford our Board a meaningful opportunity to consider the qualifications of the proposed nominees and the advisability of any other proposed business and, to the extent deemed necessary or desirable by our Board, to inform
shareholders and make recommendations about such qualifications or business, as well as to provide a more orderly procedure for conducting meetings of shareholders. Although our bylaws do not give our Board any power to disapprove shareholder
nominations for the election of directors or proposals recommending certain action, they may have the effect of precluding a contest for the election of directors or the consideration of shareholder proposals if proper procedures are not followed
and of discouraging or deterring a third party from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect its own slate of directors or to approve its own proposal without regard to whether consideration of such nominees or proposals might be harmful or
beneficial to us and our shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Calling of Special Meetings of Shareholders </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our bylaws provide that special meetings of shareholders may be called by our Board, its chairman and certain of our officers. Additionally,
our bylaws provide that, subject to the satisfaction of certain procedural and informational requirements by the shareholders requesting the meeting, a special meeting of shareholders will be called by the Fund&#8217;s secretary upon the written
request of shareholders entitled to cast not less than a majority of all the votes entitled to be cast at such meeting. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Approval of Extraordinary
Corporate Action; Amendment of Charter and Bylaws </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under Maryland law, a Maryland corporation generally cannot dissolve, amend its
charter, merge, sell all or substantially all of its assets, engage in a share exchange or engage in similar transactions outside the ordinary course of business, unless approved by the affirmative vote of shareholders entitled to cast at least <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-thirds</FONT> of the votes entitled to be cast on the matter. However, a Maryland corporation may provide in its charter for approval of these matters by a lesser percentage, but not less than a majority of all of the
votes entitled to be cast on the matter. Our charter provides that, except with respect to removal of directors, approval of certain amendments to the charter and approval of certain extraordinary actions, any action will be effective and valid if
declared advisable by the Board and taken or approved by the affirmative vote of shareholders entitled to cast a majority of all the votes entitled to be cast on the matter. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under our charter, the following extraordinary actions and amendments to the charter generally require the affirmative vote of the
shareholders entitled to cast at least 80% of the votes entitled to be cast generally in the election of directors, with holders of each class or series of shares voting as a separate class: (a)&nbsp;any amendment to the charter to make the Common
Shares &#8220;redeemable securities&#8221; and any other proposal to convert the Fund to an <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;open-end</FONT> company&#8221; (as defined in the 1940 Act); (b) the liquidation or dissolution of the Fund and any
amendment to the charter to effect such liquidation or dissolution; (c)&nbsp;any amendment to, or any amendment inconsistent with the provisions of Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.8, 7.1 or 7.2 of the charter; (d)&nbsp;any merger, consolidation, conversion,
share exchange or sale or exchange of all or substantially all of the assets of the Fund that the MGCL requires be approved by the shareholders; and (e)&nbsp;any transaction between (1)&nbsp;the Fund and (2)&nbsp;a person, or group of persons acting
together (including, without limitation, a &#8220;group&#8221; for purposes of Section&nbsp;13(d) of the Exchange Act or any successor provision) that is entitled to exercise or direct the exercise, or acquire the right to exercise or direct the
exercise, directly or indirectly, other than solely by virtue of a revocable proxy, of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-tenth</FONT> or more of the voting power in the election of directors generally, or any person controlling, controlled by or
under common control with, or employed by or acting as an agent of, any such person or member of such group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">However, if the Continuing
Directors (as defined below) of the Fund, by a vote of at least a majority of such Continuing Directors, in addition to approval by our Board, approve such proposal, transaction or amendment referred to in clauses (a)-(e) in the preceding paragraph,
the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the votes entitled to be cast on the matter will be sufficient to approve such proposal, transaction or amendment. In addition, with respect to any transaction referred to in clause (b)&nbsp;of
the preceding paragraph, if such transaction is </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Section&nbsp;2-702</FONT> of the MGCL and otherwise to the extent permitted by applicable law, our

any shareholders&#8217; derivative proceeding or other proceeding on the grounds of lack of authority, defective or irregular execution, adverse interest of a director, officer or shareholder, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-disclosure,</FONT>
miscomputation or the application of improper accounting principles or practices may be ratified, before or after judgment, by the Board or by our shareholders, and such ratification will be binding on the Fund and our shareholders and will
constitute a bar to any claim or execution of any judgment with respect to the questioned action or inaction. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Inspection of Books and Records
</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our charter provides that a shareholder who is otherwise eligible under applicable law to inspect the Fund&#8217;s books of
account, stock ledger or other specified documents has no right to make such an inspection if the Board determines that the shareholder has an improper purpose for requesting the inspection. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Exclusive Forum </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under our
charter, unless we consent in writing to the selection of a different forum, and except for any claims made under the federal U.S. securities laws, the Circuit Court for Baltimore City, Maryland (the &#8220;<U>Maryland Circuit Court</U>&#8221;), or
if the Maryland Circuit Court does not have jurisdiction, the United States District Court for the District of Maryland, Baltimore Division, will be the sole and exclusive forum for (a)&nbsp;any action asserting an internal corporate claim (as
defined in the MGCL), (b) any derivative action or proceeding brought on behalf of the Fund, (c)&nbsp;any action asserting a claim of breach of any duty owed by any director, officer or employee of the Fund to the Fund or to our shareholders,
(d)&nbsp;any action asserting a claim against the Fund or any director, officer or employee of the Fund arising pursuant to any provision of the MGCL, our charter or bylaws, or (e)&nbsp;any other action asserting a claim against the Fund or any
director or officer or other employee of the Fund that is governed by the internal affairs doctrine. Any shareholder (or beneficial owner of stock) who is a party to any action or proceeding governed by the exclusive forum provision of our charter
will be deemed to have consented to the jurisdiction of the foregoing courts solely for the purpose of adjudicating any action or proceeding governed by the exclusive forum provision of our charter. With respect to an action or proceeding in the
Maryland Circuit Court governed by the exclusive forum provision of our charter, the Fund and our shareholders (or beneficial owners of stock) will be deemed to have consented to the assignment of the action or proceeding to the Business and
Technology Case Management Program for the State of Maryland pursuant to Maryland Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">16-308</FONT> (or any successor thereof). </P>

Indemnification and Advancement of Expenses.</I>&#8221; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">So long as we are regulated under the 1940 Act, the above indemnification and

security holders to which he or she might otherwise be subject by reason of his or her willful misfeasance, bad faith, gross negligence or reckless disregard of the duties involved in the conduct of his or her office unless a determination is made
by final decision of a court, by vote of a majority of a quorum of directors who are disinterested, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-party</FONT> directors or by independent legal counsel that the liability for which indemnification is sought

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To the shareholder and the Board of Directors of Sagard Private Income Fund Inc. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Opinion on the Financial Statements </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have audited the
accompanying statement of assets and liabilities of Sagard Private Income Fund Inc. (the &#8220;Fund&#8221;) as of September&nbsp;30, 2026, the related statement of operations for the period from March&nbsp;20, 2026 (date of inception) to
September&nbsp;30, 2026, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;financial statements&#8221;). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Fund as of
September&nbsp;30, 2026, and the results of its operation for the period from March&nbsp;20, 2026 (date of inception) to September&nbsp;30, 2026, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Basis for Opinion </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These financial statements are the
responsibility of the Fund&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Fund&#8217;s financial statements based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
(United States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Fund in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB and in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States of
America. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Fund is not required to have, nor were we
engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audit, we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the
effectiveness of the Fund&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our audit included performing
procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the
amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audit also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We
believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">/s/ Deloitte&nbsp;&amp; Touche LLP </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">New York, New York </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">October&nbsp;28, 2026 </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have served as the Fund&#8217;s auditor since 2026. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Sagard Private Income Fund Inc. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="fin488260_104"></A>Notes to the Financial Statements </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note 1. Organization </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sagard Private Income Fund Inc.
(the &#8220;Fund&#8221;) was formed as a Delaware statutory trust on March&nbsp;20, 2026. On September&nbsp;18, 2026, the Fund converted from a Delaware statutory trust to a Maryland corporation and changed its legal name from &#8220;Sagard Private
Income Fund&#8221; to &#8220;Sagard Private Income Fund Inc.&#8221; The Fund was formed to originate and invest primarily in a portfolio of newly originated, privately negotiated first-lien senior secured loans to U.S. middle market companies. The
Fund expects to invest primarily in private credit investments, asset-based opportunities and broadly syndicated loans. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund is an externally
managed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-diversified,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">closed-end</FONT> management investment company that intends to elect to be regulated as a business development company (&#8220;BDC&#8221;) under the
Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;1940 Act&#8221;). In addition, following its election to be regulated as a BDC, the Fund intends to, as soon as reasonably practicable, qualify and elect to be treated for United States
(&#8220;U.S.&#8221;) federal income tax purposes as a regulated investment company (&#8220;RIC&#8221;) under Subchapter M of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;). As of September&nbsp;30, 2026, the Fund had not
commenced investment operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sagard Holdings Manager (US) LLC (the &#8220;Adviser&#8221;) is the Fund&#8217;s investment adviser. The Adviser is
indirectly wholly owned by Sagard Holdings Management Inc. (&#8220;Sagard&#8221;). Sagard Holdings Inc. (&#8220;SHI&#8221;) is the largest shareholder of Sagard and is a subsidiary of Power Corporation of Canada (&#8220;PCC&#8221;), a publicly
traded international management and holding company that focuses on financial services in North America, Europe, and Asia. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund intends to conduct a
continuous private offering of Class&nbsp;I shares of its common stock, $0.001 par value per share (the &#8220;Common Shares&#8221;), in reliance on exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note 2. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Basis of Presentation </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund&#8217;s financial
statements are prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;). The Fund is an investment company following accounting and reporting guidance in Accounting Standards
Codification Topic 946, Financial Services &#8212; Investment Companies (&#8220;ASC 946&#8221;). The Fund&#8217;s first fiscal period will end December&nbsp;31, 2026. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Use of Estimates </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of the Fund&#8217;s
financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements. Actual results could differ from those
estimates, and the differences could be material. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cash and cash equivalents represent cash held in banks and liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less. Cash and cash equivalents are
carried at cost, which approximates fair value. The Fund&#8217;s cash and cash equivalents are held with financial institutions. The Fund&#8217;s cash balances held at financial institutions may, from time to time, exceed the Federal Deposit
Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) insured limits. The Fund has not experienced any losses in such accounts and monitors the creditworthiness of the financial institutions with which it conducts business. The Fund believes it is not exposed
to any significant credit risk on cash </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Organizational and Offering Expenses </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Organizational costs are recorded as incurred, and include, without limitation, the cost of formation, including legal fees related to the creation and
organization of the Fund and its related documents of organization. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Offering expenses include, without limitation, legal, printing and other offering and
marketing costs, including the fees of professional advisors and expenses associated with the preparation of the Fund&#8217;s registration statement. Offering expenses of the Fund are capitalized as a deferred charge and amortized to expense on a
straight-line basis over 12 months from the commencement of operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the period from March&nbsp;20, 2026 (date of inception) to September&nbsp;30,
2026, the Fund incurred $1,245,143 of organizational costs (appearing as an expense on the Statement of Operations) and $841,010 of offering costs (which have been recorded as a deferred asset on the Statement of Assets and Liabilities in accordance
with Note&nbsp;3), for a total of $2,086,153. Of this amount, $586,153 was waived and will be paid directly by the Adviser in accordance with the Expense Support Agreement as it was above the Expense Cap (defined in Note 3) of $1,500,000 (this was
reflected in the Statement of Operations as an expense waiver). The difference between the organizational costs and expense waiver is $658,990. This amount is presented as an expense reimbursement in the Statement of Operations and as a Receivable
from Adviser and an Accrued Expense in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities. As of September&nbsp;30, 2026, the Fund does not consider a Reimbursement Payment (defined in Note 3) to be probable and estimable, and accordingly no liability has been
recorded. Offering costs of $841,010 are included in Accrued Expenses in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Income Taxes </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund intends to elect to be regulated as a BDC under the 1940 Act. Following its election to be regulated as a BDC, the Fund intends to, as soon as
reasonably practicable, qualify and elect to be treated as a RIC under Subchapter M of the Code. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">So long as the Fund maintains its tax status as a RIC,
it generally will not pay corporate-level U.S. federal income taxes on any ordinary income or capital gains that it distributes at least annually to its shareholders as dividends. Therefore, so long as the Fund maintains its tax status as a RIC, no
provision for U.S. federal income taxes is recorded in the financial statements of the Fund. Rather, any tax liability related to income earned and distributed by the Fund would represent obligations of the Fund&#8217;s investors. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund evaluates tax positions taken or expected to be taken in the course of preparing its financial statements to determine whether the tax positions are <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;more-likely-than-not&#8221;</FONT> to be sustained by the applicable tax authority. Tax positions not deemed to meet the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;more-likely-than-not&#8221;</FONT> threshold are
reserved and recorded as a tax benefit or expense in the current year. All penalties and interest associated with income taxes are included in income tax expense. Conclusions regarding tax positions are subject to review and may be adjusted at a
later date based on factors including, but not limited to, ongoing analyses of tax laws, regulations and interpretations thereof. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To qualify for and
maintain qualification as a RIC, the Fund must, among other things, meet certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">source-of-income</FONT></FONT> and asset diversification requirements. In addition, to qualify for RIC
tax treatment, the Fund must distribute to its shareholders, for each taxable year, at least 90% of the sum of (i)&nbsp;its &#8220;investment company taxable income&#8221; for that year (determined without regard to the deduction for dividends
paid), which is generally its net ordinary income plus the excess, if any, of its realized net short-term capital gains over its realized net long-term capital losses and (ii)&nbsp;its net <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> income,
if any. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Prior to qualifying as a RIC, the Fund is taxed as a C corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes. To qualify as a RIC for its initial RIC
taxable year, the Fund must distribute all of its accumulated earnings and profits attributable, if any, to any taxable year in which it was taxed as a C corporation. In addition, the Fund may become subject to corporate-level tax on certain <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">built-in</FONT> gains recognized during a specified period following its qualification as a RIC, unless it elects to recognize and pay tax on those <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">built-in</FONT> gains at the time of
qualification. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Segment Reporting </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund operates as a single
reportable segment. The Fund&#8217;s President and Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer collectively perform the function of the Fund&#8217;s chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) and are responsible for
allocating resources and assessing the Fund&#8217;s performance. As of September&nbsp;30, 2026, the Fund had not commenced investment operations and therefore had no operating results for the CODM to assess. The Fund&#8217;s segment assets are
reflected as total assets on the accompanying Statement of Assets and Liabilities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note 3. Agreements and Related Party Transactions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund has entered into certain agreements and transactions with the Adviser and other affiliated or related parties. The Fund is party to an Investment
Advisory Agreement with Sagard Holdings Manager (US) LLC (the &#8220;Adviser&#8221;), which was approved by the Fund&#8217;s Board of Directors at its organizational meeting on September&nbsp;18, 2026, and became effective as of September&nbsp;30,
2026 in accordance with the 1940 Act. Under the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement, the Adviser serves as the Fund&#8217;s investment adviser and is responsible for managing the investment and reinvestment of the Fund&#8217;s assets. The
Investment Advisory Agreement will remain in effect for an initial period of two years from its effective date, and thereafter will continue automatically for successive annual periods, subject to annual approval by the Board of Directors or a
majority of the outstanding voting securities of the Fund, including a majority of the independent directors. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Management Fee </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under the Investment Advisory Agreement, the Fund pays the Adviser a base management fee (the &#8220;Base Management Fee&#8221;) and an incentive fee (the
&#8220;Incentive Fee&#8221;), in each case commencing on and after the date on which the Fund elects to be regulated as a BDC (the &#8220;BDC Election Date&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Base Management Fee is calculated at an annual rate of 1.25% of the Fund&#8217;s average monthly net assets and is payable quarterly in arrears. Pursuant
to a separate fee waiver letter agreement (the &#8220;Fee Waiver Letter Agreement&#8221;), the Adviser has agreed to waive the portion of the Base Management Fee in excess of 0.85% per annum of the Fund&#8217;s average monthly net assets for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> period following the BDC Election Date, resulting in an effective annual rate of 0.85% during such period. Amounts waived under the Fee Waiver Letter Agreement are not subject to recoupment by the Adviser.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Incentive Fee </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Incentive Fee consists of two
components that are independent of each other, with the result that one component may be payable even if the other is not. A portion of the Incentive Fee is based on the Fund&#8217;s income and a portion is based on the Fund&#8217;s capital gains,
each as described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Income Incentive Fee </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The
portion of the Incentive Fee based on the Fund&#8217;s income (the &#8220;Income Incentive Fee&#8221;) is calculated and payable quarterly in arrears, commencing with the first full calendar quarter after the BDC Election Date, based
</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-7 </P>

on the Fund&#8217;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income for the immediately preceding quarter.
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; means interest income, distribution/dividend income and any other income (including any other fees (other than fees for providing managerial assistance)
such as commitment, origination, structuring, diligence and consulting fees or other fees that the Fund receives from portfolio companies) accrued during the calendar quarter, minus the Fund&#8217;s operating expenses accrued for the quarter
(including the Base Management Fee, costs and expenses payable or reimbursed to the Adviser under the administration agreement with the Adviser (the &#8220;Administration Agreement&#8221;), and any interest expense or fees on any credit facilities
or outstanding debt and dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred shares, but excluding the Incentive Fee and any shareholder servicing and/or distribution fees). <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment
Income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as market or original issue discount, debt instruments with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">payment-in-kind</FONT></FONT> interest,
preferred stock investments with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">payment-in-kind</FONT></FONT> dividends, and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">zero-coupon</FONT> securities), accrued income that the Fund has not yet
received in cash. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income does not include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation. The impact of expense support
payments and recoupments are also excluded from <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Income Incentive Fee
is subject to a quarterly hurdle rate of 1.25% (5.0% annualized), expressed as a rate of return on the value of the Fund&#8217;s net assets at the end of the most recently completed calendar quarter, subject to a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;catch-up&#8221;</FONT> feature. No Income Incentive Fee is payable in any calendar quarter in which <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income does not exceed the 1.25%
hurdle rate. The Adviser receives 100% of the dollar amount of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income exceeding the 1.25% hurdle rate but less than or equal to 1.43% (5.72% annualized) (the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;catch-up&#8221;),</FONT> and 12.5% of the dollar amount of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income, if any, that exceeds 1.43%. The
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">catch-up</FONT> is intended to provide the Adviser with approximately 12.5% of the Fund&#8217;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income as if a hurdle rate did not apply once <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Incentive</FONT> Fee Net Investment Income exceeds 1.43% in a calendar quarter. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Capital Gains Incentive Fee </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The second component of the Incentive Fee is based on the Fund&#8217;s capital gains (the &#8220;Capital Gains Incentive Fee&#8221;). The Capital Gains
Incentive Fee is determined and payable annually in arrears as of the end of each calendar year (or upon termination of the Advisory Agreement) commencing with the end of the first calendar year in which the BDC Election Date occurs. The Capital
Gains Incentive Fee will equal to 12.5% of the Fund&#8217;s cumulative realized capital gains from the BDC Election Date through the end of the applicable year, computed net of cumulative realized capital losses and cumulative unrealized capital
depreciation, less the aggregate amount of any previously paid Capital Gains Incentive Fees. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Administration Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund has entered into an Administration Agreement with the Adviser (in such capacity, the &#8220;Administrator&#8221;) under which the Administrator
provides, or oversees the provision of, administrative services. There is no separate fee paid to the Administrator for services provided under the Administration Agreement; however, the Fund reimburses the Administrator for costs and expenses
incurred in performing its obligations and providing personnel and facilities thereunder, including an allocable portion of the compensation and related expenses of certain personnel of Sagard and its affiliates providing administrative services to
the Fund on behalf of the Adviser. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Expense Support and Conditional Reimbursement Agreement </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund has entered into an Expense Support and Conditional Reimbursement Agreement (the &#8220;Expense Support Agreement&#8221;) with the Adviser. Under the
Expense Support Agreement, the Adviser (1)&nbsp;agreed to advance or otherwise bear all of the Fund&#8217;s organizational and offering expenses through December&nbsp;31, 2026 and (2)&nbsp;may elect to pay certain expenses of the Fund on the
Fund&#8217;s behalf (each, an &#8220;Expense Payment&#8221;). Expense </P>

servicing fees. In no event will the Fund bear more than $1,500,000 of organizational and offering expenses (the &#8220;Expense Cap&#8221;). To the extent such expenses exceed $1,500,000, the Adviser will pay such excess on the Fund&#8217;s behalf
without reimbursement or recoupment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Beginning after December&nbsp;31, 2026, following any calendar month in which the Fund&#8217;s Available Operating
Funds exceed cumulative distributions accrued to the Fund&#8217;s shareholders based on distributions declared with respect to record dates occurring in such month, the Fund is required, subject to the conditions of the Expense Support Agreement, to
reimburse the Adviser for eligible unreimbursed Expense Payments made by the Adviser within the preceding three years (each, a &#8220;Reimbursement Payment&#8221;). &#8220;Available Operating Funds&#8221; means the sum of (i)&nbsp;the Fund&#8217;s
net investment income calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP, (ii)&nbsp;the Fund&#8217;s net capital gains (including the excess of net long-term capital gains over net short-term capital losses) and (iii)&nbsp;dividends and other distributions
received by the Fund from portfolio companies, to the extent such amounts are not otherwise included in clauses (i)&nbsp;or (ii). The amount of any Reimbursement Payment is limited to the lesser of such excess Available Operating Funds for the
applicable calendar month and the aggregate amount of eligible unreimbursed Expense Payments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">No Reimbursement Payment may be made in an applicable
calendar month if the Fund&#8217;s Operating Expense Ratio at the time of the proposed Reimbursement Payment is greater than the Operating Expense Ratio at the time the related Expense Payment was made. &#8220;Operating Expense Ratio&#8221; means
the Fund&#8217;s operating expenses, excluding organizational and offering expenses, Base Management Fees, Incentive Fees, shareholder servicing and/or distribution fees and interest expense, divided by the Fund&#8217;s monthly average net assets.

into a Trademark License Agreement (the &#8220;License Agreement&#8221;) with Sagard Holdings Manager LP (the &#8220;Licensor&#8221;), pursuant to which the Fund has been granted a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-exclusive</FONT> license to use
the name &#8220;Sagard&#8221;. The License Agreement remains in effect only for so long as the Adviser or one of its affiliates remains the Fund&#8217;s investment adviser, and either party may terminate it at any time on 60 days&#8217; written
notice. The Licensor may also terminate it immediately upon written notice if it receives notice of a third-party infringement claim arising from the Fund&#8217;s use of the name or if the Fund assigns or sublicenses its rights without consent. Upon
termination, the Fund would be required to discontinue use of the name &#8220;Sagard.&#8221; Other than under this limited license, the Fund has no legal right to the &#8220;Sagard&#8221; name. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note 4. Share Repurchase Program </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Beginning no later than
the quarter ending June&nbsp;30, 2027, the Fund intends to commence a discretionary share repurchase program pursuant to which it intends, subject to market conditions and the discretion of its Board of Directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;), to offer
to repurchase in each quarter up to 5% of its Common Shares outstanding as of the close of the previous calendar quarter. To the extent the Fund offers to repurchase Common Shares in any particular quarter, the Fund expects to repurchase such shares
at a price equal to net asset value (&#8220;NAV&#8221;) per share as of the last calendar day of a&nbsp;month designated by the Board during the applicable quarter. The Board may amend, suspend or terminate the share repurchase program in its
discretion, subject to applicable law. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Note 5. Commitments and Contingencies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the normal course of business, the Fund may enter into contracts that provide a variety of general indemnifications. Any exposure to the Fund under these
arrangements could involve future claims that may be made against the Fund. As of September&nbsp;30, 2026, no such claims exist or are expected to arise, and accordingly, the Fund has not accrued any liability in connection with such
indemnifications.</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>SPV Contribution and Initial Portfolio </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund
commenced investment operations in connection with the closing of a contribution transaction on October&nbsp;27, 2026 (the &#8220;<U>SPV Contribution</U>&#8221;), after which the Fund expects to file its election to be treated as a BDC under the
1940 Act. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the SPV Contribution, the Fund acquired all of the limited partnership interests of Sagard Private Income Fund SPV I LP
(&#8220;<U>SPV I</U>&#8221;), a special purpose vehicle formed as a Delaware limited partnership in May 2026, which holds a portfolio of U.S. dollar-denominated, first-lien senior secured direct lending investments and which comprises the
Fund&#8217;s initial investment portfolio (the &#8220;<U>Initial Portfolio</U>&#8221;). In connection with the SPV Contribution, the Fund also acquired all of the equity interests in SPV I&#8217;s general partner. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Initial Portfolio has been originated and managed by investment personnel of the Adviser and consists of investments consistent with the Fund&#8217;s
investment objective and strategy. The aggregate purchase price for the limited partnership interests of SPV I in the SPV Contribution was approximately $76.5&nbsp;million, which is equal to the NAV of SPV I as of closing of the SPV Contribution.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In exchange for the SPV Contribution, SHI&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiary, Sagard Holdings Investment I LP, received approximately 7,654,277 Class&nbsp;I
shares, which amount equals the net asset value of SPV I divided by the then-current NAV per Common Share, as determined in accordance with the Fund&#8217;s valuation policies and procedures. </P>

administrative agent (&#8220;<U>Atlas</U>&#8221;), Atlas Securitized Products, L.P., as lead arranger, U.S. </P>
